details.title: The Expanding Universe
details.scientificExplanation: The expansion of the universe is a fundamental discovery of modern cosmology. In 1929, Edwin Hubble observed that galaxies are moving away from each other, with speeds proportional to their distance, which led to the formulation of Hubble's Law. This observation supported the Big Bang theory, which states that the universe began approximately 13.8 billion years ago from a singular point. Expansion means that space itself is stretching, increasing the distance between galaxies. In 1998, observations of Type Ia supernovae revealed that this expansion is accelerating, a phenomenon attributed to dark energy, which represents about 68% of the energy density of the universe. The cosmic microwave background radiation, discovered in 1965, provides additional evidence of expansion, showing a thermal image of the early universe.
details.arabicVerse: وَالسَّمَاءَ بَنَيْنَاهَا بِأَيْدٍ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ
details.verseTranslation: And the heaven, We constructed it with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander.
details.verseCommentary: This verse uses the Arabic term 'musi'un' (موسعون), meaning 'those who expand'. This description corresponds to the modern discovery of the universe's expansion, where space is continuously stretching, a concept unknown in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, cosmological concepts described a static universe. Greek philosophers like Aristotle believed the heavens were fixed. The idea of an expanding universe only emerged in the 20th century with Einstein and Hubble, making the Quranic description remarkable.

timeline.event: The Quran reveals the expansive nature of the universe.
Einstein publishes general relativity, predicting a dynamic universe.
Hubble discovers the recession of galaxies.
Discovery of accelerated expansion due to dark energy.

details.title: Relativity and Time Dilation
details.scientificExplanation: Time dilation is a key concept in Albert Einstein's special and general relativity. According to special relativity (1905), time slows down for an observer in motion relative to a stationary observer, a phenomenon measurable at speeds close to that of light. General relativity (1915) shows that time also slows down in strong gravitational fields, such as near a black hole. These effects have been confirmed by experiments, like atomic clocks on GPS satellites, which run slightly faster due to weaker gravity. Time dilation challenges the classical notion of absolute time, revealing that time is relative to speed and gravity.
details.arabicVerse: يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ
details.verseTranslation: He manages the affairs from the heaven to the earth, then they ascend to Him in a day whose measure is a thousand years of your reckoning.
details.verseCommentary: This verse refers to a day equivalent to a thousand years, suggesting a relative perception of time. This idea corresponds to time dilation, where time can vary according to physical conditions, a concept unknown at the time of the Quran's revelation.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, time was considered absolute and universal across all cultures. Einstein's work in the 20th century revolutionized this understanding, showing that time is relative. The Quranic mention of temporal variability is therefore notable for its era.

timeline.event: The Quran alludes to the relativity of time.
Einstein publishes special relativity, introducing time dilation.
Einstein publishes general relativity, linking time and gravity.

details.title: Atomic Structure
details.scientificExplanation: Atomic structure is at the heart of modern chemistry and physics. John Dalton proposed in 1803 that matter is composed of indivisible atoms. Later, J.J. Thomson (1897) discovered the electron, and Ernest Rutherford (1911) established the atomic model with a central nucleus surrounded by electrons. Quantum mechanics refined this model, revealing that atoms are made of protons, neutrons, and electrons, with even smaller subatomic particles like quarks. Atoms are incredibly small, with a diameter of about 0.1 nanometers, yet they form the basis of all visible matter.
details.arabicVerse: وَمَا يَعْزُبُ عَن رَّبِّكَ مِن مِّثْقَالِ ذَرَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ
details.verseTranslation: Nothing escapes your Lord, not even the weight of a particle on earth or in heaven.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'dharra' (ذرة) in this verse refers to a minute particle, often interpreted as the smallest unit of matter. This description anticipates the discovery of atoms, entities so small they were inconceivable in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, ideas about matter were rudimentary. Greek philosophers like Democritus had speculated about indivisible particles, but without experimental evidence. The modern understanding of atomic structure only emerged in the 19th century, making the Quranic reference significant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions 'dharra', a minute particle.
Dalton proposes the modern atomic theory.
Thomson discovers the electron.
Rutherford establishes the nuclear atomic model.

details.title: Hints of Quantum Mechanics
details.scientificExplanation: Quantum mechanics, developed in the early 20th century, describes the behavior of matter and energy at subatomic scales. Max Planck (1900) introduced the idea that energy is emitted in discrete quanta, and Werner Heisenberg (1925) formulated the uncertainty principle, showing that certain properties, like the position and velocity of a particle, cannot be measured simultaneously with precision. Wave-particle duality and quantum entanglement reveal a world where invisible realities defy classical intuition. These concepts are fundamental to modern technologies like lasers and quantum computers.
details.arabicVerse: وَعِندَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ
details.verseTranslation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'ghayb' (unseen) in this verse can be interpreted as encompassing the subatomic realities studied by quantum mechanics. This reference to hidden knowledge corresponds to the discovery of invisible phenomena that govern the universe.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, there was no understanding of subatomic phenomena. Scientific advances in the 20th century, particularly the work of Planck, Einstein, and Schrödinger, revealed an invisible world, making the Quranic mention of the unseen relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran refers to the unseen ('ghayb').
Planck introduces quantum theory.
Heisenberg formulates the uncertainty principle.
Einstein, Podolsky, and Rosen describe quantum entanglement.

details.title: Black Holes
details.scientificExplanation: Black holes are regions of space where gravity is so intense that not even light can escape. Predicted by Einstein's general relativity, they were theorized by Karl Schwarzschild in 1916. Black holes often form from the collapse of massive stars. Their presence is detected indirectly through effects like matter accretion or gravitational waves, first observed in 2015 by LIGO. In 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope captured the first image of a black hole in galaxy M87, confirming their existence.
details.arabicVerse: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ
details.verseTranslation: I swear by the receding stars, those that move and disappear.
details.verseCommentary: The terms 'khunnas' (those that recede) and 'kunnas' (those that disappear) can be interpreted as describing invisible celestial objects or those that absorb light, similar to black holes, which were inconceivable in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, astronomical observations were limited to the naked eye, and concepts of invisible celestial objects were absent. The Quranic description of celestial bodies that 'disappear' anticipates modern discoveries of black holes.

timeline.event: The Quran describes celestial objects that disappear.
Schwarzschild proposes a solution for black holes.
LIGO detects gravitational waves from a black hole merger.
First image of a black hole by the Event Horizon Telescope.

details.title: Cosmic Radiation
details.scientificExplanation: Cosmic rays are high-energy particles, mainly protons and atomic nuclei, traveling at speeds close to that of light. Discovered by Victor Hess in 1912, they come from sources like supernovae and black holes. Earth's atmosphere acts as a shield, protecting life by absorbing and scattering these rays. Earth's magnetic field also deflects charged particles, reducing their impact. Cosmic rays influence climate and genetic mutations, playing a role in evolution.
details.arabicVerse: وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَّحْفُوظًا
details.verseTranslation: And We made the sky a protected roof.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'protected roof' (saqfan mahfuzan) can be interpreted as referring to Earth's atmosphere, which protects life from harmful cosmic rays, a function confirmed by modern science.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, there was no knowledge of cosmic rays or the protective function of the atmosphere. Modern scientific observations have revealed the importance of the atmosphere as a shield, making this Quranic description remarkable.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the sky as a 'protected roof'.

details.title: Conservation of Energy
details.scientificExplanation: The law of conservation of energy states that the total energy of an isolated system remains constant, although it may transform from one form to another (e.g., kinetic to thermal). Stated by Hermann von Helmholtz in 1847, it is a fundamental principle of physics. This law applies to all natural processes, from chemical reactions to planetary movements. The energy balance of the universe, including dark energy and matter, maintains the observed cosmic stability.
details.arabicVerse: وَالسَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ
details.verseTranslation: And the heaven He raised and established the balance.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'mizan' (balance) suggests a cosmic order where everything is maintained in balance, which corresponds to the conservation of energy, a concept where total energy remains constant in a closed system.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, energy concepts were not formalized. Natural philosophers discussed forces, but without quantitative understanding. The modern formulation of energy conservation in the 19th century makes the Quranic reference to balance remarkable.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions cosmic balance ('mizan').
Helmholtz formulates the law of conservation of energy.
Einstein relates mass and energy with E=mc².

details.title: Electromagnetic Waves
details.scientificExplanation: Electromagnetic waves, described by James Clerk Maxwell in 1865, encompass a spectrum ranging from radio waves to gamma rays. These waves are oscillations of electric and magnetic fields propagating at the speed of light. Heinrich Hertz confirmed their existence in 1887 through experiments. Electromagnetic waves are essential to modern technologies like radio, television, and telecommunications. Their invisible nature, except for visible light, corresponds to the Quranic description of subtle luminous phenomena.
details.arabicVerse: اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ
details.verseTranslation: Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'nur' (light) can be interpreted as encompassing electromagnetic waves, which include visible and invisible light. This description is consistent with the scientific discovery of electromagnetic waves, unknown in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, light was perceived as a visible phenomenon, without understanding of invisible waves. The work of Maxwell and Hertz in the 19th century revealed the electromagnetic nature of light, making the Quranic reference significant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes Allah as the light of the heavens and earth.
Maxwell formulates the equations of electromagnetic waves.
Hertz experimentally confirms electromagnetic waves.

details.title: Dark Matter
details.scientificExplanation: Dark matter is a hypothetical form of matter that neither radiates nor absorbs light but exerts gravitational influence. Proposed by Fritz Zwicky in 1933 to explain anomalies in galaxy movements, it represents about 27% of the energy density of the universe. Observations of galactic rotation curves by Vera Rubin in the 1970s strengthened this hypothesis. Dark matter cannot be detected directly, but its effect is visible in galaxy formation and the cosmic background.
details.arabicVerse: ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ
details.verseTranslation: Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'dukhan' (smoke) can be interpreted as a reference to a diffuse and invisible substance, similar to dark matter, which plays a crucial role in the formation of the universe, a concept unknown in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, there was no notion of invisible matter influencing gravity. Modern discoveries of dark matter, based on indirect observations, make the Quranic description of 'dukhan' significant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the heaven as 'smoke'.
Zwicky proposes the existence of dark matter.

details.title: Big Bang Theory
details.scientificExplanation: The Big Bang theory, proposed by Georges Lemaître in 1927, postulates that the universe began approximately 13.8 billion years ago from an extremely dense and hot singular point. The expansion observed by Hubble in 1929 supported this theory. The cosmic microwave background radiation, discovered in 1965 by Penzias and Wilson, is an imprint of the early universe. Observations of primordial nucleosynthesis and galaxy distribution confirm that the universe evolved from an initial unique state.
details.arabicVerse: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا
details.verseTranslation: Have those who disbelieved not seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them?
details.verseCommentary: The terms 'ratq' (joined entity) and 'fataq' (separated) describe an initial unified state followed by separation, which corresponds to the Big Bang theory, where the universe began as a singularity before expanding.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, cosmologies often described an eternal and static universe. The idea of a unique beginning was only formalized in the 20th century with Lemaître and Hubble, making the Quranic description of an initial separation remarkable.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the heavens and earth as a separated mass.

Discovery of cosmic microwave background radiation.

details.title: Orbital Mechanics
details.scientificExplanation: Orbital mechanics describes the movements of celestial bodies according to Newton's laws of gravitation, formulated in 1687, and Einstein's general relativity (1915). Planets, moons, and stars follow precise orbits determined by gravity. For example, Earth orbits the Sun in about 365.25 days, and the Moon around Earth in about 27.3 days. These movements are predictable and stable, ensuring that the Sun and Moon follow distinct trajectories, preventing any collision.
details.arabicVerse: لَا الشَّمْسُ يَنبَغِي لَهَا أَن تُدْرِكَ الْقَمَرَ وَلَا اللَّيْلُ سَابِقُ النَّهَارِ
details.verseTranslation: It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day.
details.verseCommentary: This verse emphasizes that the Sun and Moon follow distinct and ordered trajectories, which corresponds to orbital mechanics where each celestial body has a specific orbit, preventing any overlap or collision, an advanced concept for the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, astronomical observations were limited, and geocentric models dominated. The understanding of orbits as precise gravitational trajectories was only established with the work of Kepler and Newton, making the Quranic description of celestial trajectories notable.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the distinct trajectories of the Sun and Moon.

details.title: Star Formation
details.scientificExplanation: Stars form in nebulae, clouds of gas and dust, through gravitational collapse. When a dense region collapses, it heats up and forms a protostar, which becomes a star when nuclear fusion begins, producing light and heat. This process, studied by astronomers like Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin in the 1920s, takes millions of years. Massive stars can evolve into supernovae, while stars like the Sun end as white dwarfs.
details.arabicVerse: وَالسَّمَاءِ وَالطَّارِقِ وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الطَّارِقُ النَّجْمُ الثَّاقِبُ
details.verseTranslation: By the sky and the night comer. And what can make you know what the night comer is? It is the piercing star.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'najm thaqib' (piercing star) can be interpreted as describing a bright star or intense luminous phenomenon, corresponding to the nature of forming stars or supernovae, whose light pierces the cosmic darkness.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, stars were observed as fixed luminous points, without understanding of their formation. Modern discoveries about stellar nucleosynthesis and nebulae make the Quranic description of a 'piercing' star significant.

details.title: Black Holes and Pulsars
details.scientificExplanation: Black holes, predicted by Einstein's general relativity in 1916 by Karl Schwarzschild, are regions where gravity is so intense that nothing, not even light, can escape. Pulsars, discovered by Jocelyn Bell in 1967, are rapidly rotating neutron stars emitting regular pulses of radiation. Black holes are detected by their gravitational effects, and pulsars by their radio signals. In 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope captured the first image of a black hole.
details.arabicVerse: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ
details.verseTranslation: I swear by the receding stars, those that move and disappear.
details.verseCommentary: The terms 'khunnas' (those that recede) and 'kunnas' (those that disappear) can describe celestial objects like black holes, which are invisible, or pulsars, whose periodic signals appear to 'recede'. These descriptions correspond to phenomena discovered recently.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, concepts of invisible or pulsating celestial objects were absent. Modern observations of black holes and pulsars, requiring advanced technologies, make the Quranic description remarkable.

timeline.event: The Quran describes stars that recede and disappear.

details.title: Solar Apex
details.scientificExplanation: The solar apex refers to the Sun's movement through the Milky Way, at about 20 km/s toward the constellation Hercules, near the star Vega. Discovered in the 18th century by William Herschel, this movement reflects the Sun's orbit around the galactic center, which takes about 230 million years. This displacement is relative to the local standard of rest of neighboring stars.
details.arabicVerse: وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَّهَا
details.verseTranslation: And the sun runs [on course] toward its stopping point.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'mustaqarr' (stopping point) suggests that the Sun has a determined trajectory, which corresponds to its orbital movement around the galactic center, a concept unknown in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the Sun was often perceived as fixed or following a simple diurnal cycle. The discovery of its galactic movement by Herschel and modern observations of the galactic orbit make the Quranic description significant.

details.title: Lunar Phases
details.scientificExplanation: Lunar phases are caused by the relative positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon, leading to variations in the Moon's appearance as seen from Earth. These phases (new moon, first quarter, full moon, last quarter) follow a cycle of about 29.5 days, called the synodic month. This phenomenon is due to the changing angle of solar illumination on the Moon, observed from Earth. Ancient and modern astronomers have used these cycles for calendars and navigation.
details.arabicVerse: وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ حَتَّىٰ عَادَ كَالْعُرْجُونِ الْقَدِيمِ
details.verseTranslation: And the moon - We have determined for it phases, until it returns [appearing] like the old date stalk.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'manazil' (phases) and the comparison with an 'old date stalk' precisely describe the cycle of lunar phases, from full moon to new moon, a phenomenon observable but not fully scientifically understood in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, lunar cycles were observed for calendars, but their physical cause (solar illumination) was not explained. The Quranic description of phases as an ordered cycle reflects an advanced understanding for the time.

timeline.event: The Quran describes lunar phases as an ordered cycle.

details.title: Cosmic Dome
details.scientificExplanation: The 'cosmic dome' can be interpreted as Earth's atmosphere, which acts as a protective shield against solar radiation, cosmic rays, and meteors. Discovered in the 20th century, the atmosphere absorbs ultraviolet rays via the ozone layer and scatters cosmic rays. Earth's magnetic field also deflects charged particles, protecting life on Earth. These mechanisms are essential for maintaining a habitable environment.
details.arabicVerse: وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَّحْفُوظًا
details.verseTranslation: And We made the sky a protected ceiling.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'saqfan mahfuzan' (protected ceiling) describes the atmosphere as a protective barrier, a function confirmed by modern science which identifies the atmosphere as essential for preserving life on Earth.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the atmosphere was not recognized as a protective layer. Scientific discoveries about the ozone layer and Earth's magnetic field in the 20th century make the Quranic description of a 'protected ceiling' remarkable.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the sky as a 'protected ceiling'.

details.title: Galactic Orbits
details.scientificExplanation: Galaxies, like the Milky Way, follow gravitational trajectories influenced by dark matter and interactions with other galaxies. Stars and stellar systems orbit the galactic center, a process described by Newton's laws and refined by general relativity. Modern observations, especially via the Hubble telescope, show that galaxies follow structured 'paths', often spiral or elliptical, in the expanding universe.
details.arabicVerse: وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الْحُبُكِ
details.verseTranslation: By the heaven full of paths.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'hubuk' (paths) evokes ordered paths in the sky, which corresponds to the structured galactic orbits observed in galaxies, a concept unknown in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, galaxies were not recognized as distinct systems. Modern observations, beginning with Edwin Hubble in the 1920s, revealed the structure and movement of galaxies, making the Quranic description of 'paths' significant.

details.title: Shooting Stars
details.scientificExplanation: Shooting stars are meteors, fragments of rocks or dust entering Earth's atmosphere and burning due to friction, producing luminous trails. These events, observed since antiquity, are often associated with meteor showers like the Perseids. Earth's atmosphere acts as a barrier, incinerating most meteors before they reach the ground, thus protecting the Earth's surface.
details.arabicVerse: وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا بِمَصَابِيحَ وَجَعَلْنَاهَا رُجُومًا لِّلشَّيَاطِينِ

details.verseCommentary: The term 'masabih' (lamps) describes stars as luminous sources, while 'rujuman' (projectiles) can be interpreted as meteors burning in the atmosphere, a phenomenon perceived as cosmic protection in the Quranic context.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, meteors were observed but their nature (space debris burning in the atmosphere) was not understood. The Quranic description of stars as 'projectiles' reflects a poetic yet accurate understanding of this phenomenon.

timeline.event: The Quran describes stars as lamps and projectiles.

details.title: Interstellar Dust
details.scientificExplanation: Interstellar dust, composed of microscopic particles of carbon, silicates, and other materials, is a key component of nebulae. Observed in infrared spectra since the 20th century, it plays a role in star and planet formation by facilitating gravitational collapse. Interstellar dust absorbs and scatters light, creating dark nebulae visible in galaxies, like the Coalsack Nebula.
details.arabicVerse: ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ
details.verseTranslation: Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'dukhan' (smoke) can be interpreted as a description of interstellar dust, a diffuse substance present in the early universe, essential to the formation of cosmic structures.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the notion of cosmic dust was unknown. Modern observations, especially by infrared telescopes, have revealed the importance of interstellar dust, making the Quranic reference to cosmic 'smoke' significant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the heaven as 'smoke'.
Discovery of interstellar dust via spectroscopy.

Detailed observations of nebulae by the Spitzer telescope.

details.title: Iron from Space
details.scientificExplanation: Modern science has established that iron on Earth primarily comes from extraterrestrial sources, notably meteorites and supernovae. Iron atoms are formed in the cores of massive stars through nuclear fusion and dispersed into space during supernova explosions. Analyses of meteorites, studied since the 19th century, confirm that terrestrial iron has a cosmic origin, with isotopes distinct from stellar processes. This discovery highlights the importance of cosmic events in Earth's chemical composition.
details.arabicVerse: وَأَنزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ
details.verseTranslation: And We sent down iron, wherein is great strength.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'anzalna' (sent down) suggests an external origin for iron, aligning with the scientific discovery that iron comes from stellar and meteoritic processes, a concept unknown in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, iron was used for tools and weapons, but its cosmic origin was unknown. Modern isotope analyses and the understanding of stellar nucleosynthesis, developed in the 20th century, make the Quranic description of iron being 'sent down' remarkable.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions iron as 'sent down'.
Analysis of meteorites reveals their iron content.
Theory of stellar nucleosynthesis explains iron formation.
Confirmation of terrestrial iron's cosmic origin via spectroscopy.

details.title: Atmospheric Layers
details.scientificExplanation: Earth's atmosphere consists of several layers (troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere, exosphere), each with specific functions. The stratosphere contains the ozone layer, which absorbs ultraviolet rays, while the magnetosphere deflects charged particles from cosmic rays. Discovered in the 20th century, these layers protect life by filtering harmful radiation and burning incoming meteors.
details.arabicVerse: وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا
details.verseTranslation: And We made the sky a protected ceiling.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'saqfan mahfuzan' (protected ceiling) describes the atmosphere as a protective barrier, corresponding to the function of atmospheric layers that preserve life on Earth by blocking radiation and space debris.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the atmosphere was not recognized as a multi-layered protective system. Modern discoveries about the ozone layer and Earth's magnetic field make this Quranic description significant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the sky as a 'protected ceiling'.
Discovery of the ozone layer absorbing UV rays.
Discovery of the Van Allen belts protecting against charged particles.
Advanced studies on atmospheric layer dynamics.

details.title: Law of Gravity
details.scientificExplanation: The law of universal gravitation, formulated by Isaac Newton in 1687, states that every mass attracts another with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. This law explains planetary and stellar orbits. Einstein's general relativity (1915) refined this by describing gravity as the curvature of spacetime. Observations of planetary orbits and gravitational lensing confirm these theories.
details.arabicVerse: اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا
details.verseTranslation: It is Allah who erected the heavens without pillars that you can see.
details.verseCommentary: The phrase 'without visible pillars' suggests an invisible force holding the heavens, corresponding to gravity—an unseen but essential force maintaining celestial bodies in place.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, gravity was not conceptualized as a universal force. Cosmological models, like Ptolemy's, assumed physical spheres. The Newtonian and Einsteinian understanding of gravity makes the Quranic description without 'visible pillars' remarkable.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the heavens held without visible pillars.
Newton publishes the law of universal gravitation.
Einstein introduces general relativity.
Confirmation of general relativity by light deflection observation.

details.videoTitle: Law of Gravity: Quran and Modern Physics

details.title: Energy Balance
details.scientificExplanation: The law of energy conservation, formulated by Hermann von Helmholtz in 1847, states that the total energy of an isolated system remains constant, transforming from one form to another (kinetic, thermal, potential). This law applies to the universe, where total energy, including dark energy, maintains cosmic balance. Observations of the universe, like the accelerated expansion discovered in 1998, confirm this global energy balance.
details.arabicVerse: وَالسَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ
details.verseTranslation: And the heaven He raised and imposed the balance.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'mizan' (balance) evokes a cosmic order where energy is conserved, corresponding to the scientific law of energy conservation, essential for the universe's stability.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, energy concepts were absent from human knowledge. The formalization of energy conservation in the 19th century makes the Quranic reference to cosmic 'balance' significant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions cosmic balance ('mizan').
Helmholtz formulates the law of energy conservation.
Einstein relates mass and energy with E=mc².
Discovery of accelerated expansion linked to dark energy.

details.title: Light Reflection
details.scientificExplanation: Light reflection is an optical principle where light bounces off a surface, following the law of reflection (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection). Described by Ibn al-Haytham in the 11th century and formalized by Snell and Descartes in the 17th century, this property is essential for mirrors, telescopes, and other optical technologies. Visible light, a small part of the electromagnetic spectrum, is reflected by smooth surfaces like glass or metals.
details.arabicVerse: اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ
details.verseTranslation: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'nur' (light) can include visible light, whose reflection is a fundamental phenomenon. This poetic description aligns with modern optical principles of light reflection, discovered long after the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, light was perceived as a visible phenomenon without understanding optical laws. The works of Ibn al-Haytham and modern scientists on reflection make the Quranic reference to light significant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes Allah as the light of the heavens and earth.
Ibn al-Haytham develops the foundations of modern optics.
Snell formulates the law of reflection.
Development of optical technologies like telescopes.

details.title: Sound Waves
details.scientificExplanation: Sound waves are mechanical vibrations propagating through a medium, like air, as pressure variations. Studied by Robert Boyle in the 17th century and later formalized, they travel at about 343 m/s in air at room temperature. Sound is essential for communication and used in technologies like ultrasound. The Quranic verse, though metaphorical, can be linked to sound propagation in the atmosphere.
details.arabicVerse: يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ النَّهَارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ
details.verseTranslation: He causes the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night.
details.verseCommentary: Though metaphorical, this description of the smooth transition between night and day can be interpreted as evoking physical phenomena, like sound wave propagation in the atmosphere, accompanying day-night transitions.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, sound was perceived as an audible phenomenon without understanding its wave nature. Scientific works from the 17th century onward on sound waves make this Quranic reference relevant in a modern context.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the transition of day and night.
Boyle studies sound propagation in air.
Formalization of sound waves as mechanical vibrations.
Development of sound wave-based technologies like ultrasound.

details.title: Magnetic Fields
details.scientificExplanation: Magnetic fields are invisible forces generated by the movement of electric charges, as in magnets or Earth's magnetic field. Discovered by William Gilbert in 1600 and formalized by Maxwell in the 19th century, they deflect charged particles, as in the Van Allen belts, protecting Earth from cosmic rays. These fields are essential for technologies like electric motors and MRI.
details.arabicVerse: وَعِندَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ
details.verseTranslation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'ghayb' (unseen) can include invisible forces like magnetic fields, which influence particles and protect Earth, a concept discovered long after the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, invisible forces like magnetism were not understood. Discoveries by Gilbert and Maxwell on magnetic fields make the Quranic reference to the unseen relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions the keys of the unseen ('ghayb').
Gilbert describes Earth's magnetic field.
Maxwell unifies electricity and magnetism.
Discovery of the Van Allen belts.

details.title: Thermal Energy
details.scientificExplanation: Thermal energy is the energy associated with particle motion in a system, measured as temperature. Studied by Joule and Kelvin in the 19th century, it is transferred via conduction, convection, or radiation. Thermal energy is essential in natural processes, like solar heat warming Earth, and in technologies like heat engines. The verse, though metaphorical, can evoke heat-related phenomena.
details.arabicVerse: يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنسَانُ مَا سَعَىٰ
details.verseTranslation: The Day when man will remember that for which he strove.
details.verseCommentary: Though contextually metaphorical, the reference to human effort can be linked to thermal energy, as physical processes like human work generate heat, a concept explored scientifically later.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, heat was perceived as a sensation without understanding thermal energy. 19th-century thermodynamics works make this Quranic connection relevant in a scientific framework.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions human effort, metaphorically linked to energy.
Joule establishes the relationship between work and heat.
Kelvin develops thermodynamics.
Applications of thermal energy in modern engines.

details.title: Particle Physics
details.scientificExplanation: Particle physics studies the fundamental constituents of matter, like quarks and leptons, and their interactions via fundamental forces. Developed in the 20th century with discoveries like the electron (Thomson, 1897) and the standard model (1970s), it uses accelerators like the LHC to explore subatomic particles. These particles, smaller than 10^-15 meters, form the basis of all visible matter.
details.arabicVerse: وَمَا يَعْزُبُ عَن رَّبِّكَ مِن مِّثْقَالِ ذَرَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ
details.verseTranslation: And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'dharra' (particle) denotes a minute entity, corresponding to the notion of subatomic particles discovered by modern physics, a concept inconceivable in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, matter was perceived as continuous, without the notion of subatomic particles. 20th-century discoveries of quarks and leptons make the Quranic reference to a 'particle' significant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions the 'dharra', a minute particle.
Thomson discovers the electron.
Development of the standard model of particles.
Discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC.

details.title: Relativistic Effects
details.scientificExplanation: Relativistic effects, described by Einstein's special (1905) and general (1915) relativity, include time dilation, where time slows for a moving observer or in a strong gravitational field. Confirmed by experiments like Hafele-Keating (1971) and GPS clock corrections, these effects show time is relative, challenging the classical notion of absolute time.
details.arabicVerse: يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ
details.verseTranslation: He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count.
details.verseCommentary: The mention of a day equaling a thousand years suggests temporal variability, corresponding to relativistic time dilation, a concept unknown in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, time was considered absolute. Einstein's theories and modern experiments on relativity make this Quranic description of time variability remarkable.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions temporal variability.
Einstein publishes general relativity.
Hafele-Keating experiment confirms time dilation.

details.title: Discovery of the Water Cycle
details.scientificExplanation: The water cycle is a continuous process involving evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and runoff. Water evaporates from oceans and land, condenses into clouds, falls as rain or snow, then returns to oceans via rivers and groundwater. Described scientifically by Bernard Palissy in the 16th century and formalized in the 17th century, it is essential for sustaining life on Earth and regulating climate.
details.arabicVerse: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً
details.verseTranslation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky?
details.verseCommentary: The verse mentions water descending from the sky, a direct reference to precipitation, a key component of the water cycle, a concept not systematically understood in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, water cycle processes were not fully understood. Modern observations of the hydrological cycle, starting with Palissy, make the Quranic description of water descending from the sky significant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes water descending from the sky.
Palissy proposes a description of the water cycle.
Pierre Perrault quantifies water runoff.
Formalization of the modern hydrological cycle.

details.title: Cloud Formation
details.scientificExplanation: Cloud formation results from the cooling of humid air, causing water vapor to condense into droplets or ice crystals. Winds transport humid air to cooler altitudes, where condensation occurs, forming clouds. This process, studied by John Dalton in the 18th century, is essential for precipitation. Clouds, like cumulus or nimbus, vary based on atmospheric conditions.
details.arabicVerse: اللَّهُ الَّذِي يُرْسِلُ الرِّيَاحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابًا
details.verseTranslation: It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds.
details.verseCommentary: The verse describes winds raising clouds, corresponding to the scientific process where winds transport moisture to form clouds, a key mechanism in modern meteorology.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, cloud formation was observed but not scientifically explained. Modern works on condensation and atmospheric dynamics make the Quranic description precise.

timeline.event: The Quran describes winds raising clouds.
Dalton studies condensation and cloud formation.
Development of modern meteorology.
Advanced cloud forecasting models via satellites.

details.title: Rain and Vegetation
details.scientificExplanation: Rain provides the water necessary for photosynthesis, enabling plant growth. This process, studied by Joseph Priestley in the 18th century, involves root absorption of water, which, combined with carbon dioxide and sunlight, produces energy for plant growth. Rain plays a key role in ecosystems, supporting forests, crops, and biodiversity.
details.arabicVerse: وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً مُّبَارَكًا فَأَنبَتْنَا بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ
details.verseTranslation: And We send down blessed rain from the sky and make grow thereby gardens.
details.verseCommentary: The verse directly links rain to garden growth, reflecting water's essential role in photosynthesis and plant growth, a connection understood scientifically much later.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, rain was associated with fertility, but its role in photosynthesis was unknown. Modern discoveries on photosynthesis make the Quranic description relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran links rain to garden growth.
Priestley discovers water's role in photosynthesis.

details.title: Mountains and Stability
details.scientificExplanation: Mountains contribute to the stability of Earth's crust through their deep roots extending into the mantle. This concept, called isostasy, was developed in the 19th century by George Airy. Mountains, formed by plate tectonics, reduce crustal oscillations by balancing gravitational forces, contributing to geological stability.
details.arabicVerse: وَأَلْقَىٰ فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ
details.verseTranslation: And He has cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it shift with you.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'rawasiya' (firmly set mountains) and the idea of preventing shifting ('tamida') correspond to the function of mountain roots in isostasy, stabilizing Earth's crust.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, mountains were seen as fixed structures, but their role in geological stability was unknown. Discoveries on isostasy and plate tectonics make the Quranic description significant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes mountains as stabilizers.
Airy proposes the concept of isostasy.
Wegener develops plate tectonics theory.
Confirmation of isostasy through geophysical studies.

details.title: Rivers and Valleys
details.scientificExplanation: Rivers and valleys are formed by water erosion, where rainwater flows along natural slopes, carving out valleys and transporting sediments. This process, studied by geomorphologists in the 19th century, also includes underground rivers in karst regions, where water infiltrates the ground. These hydrological systems are essential for water supply and landscape formation.
details.arabicVerse: أَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَسَالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِهَا
details.verseTranslation: He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their capacity.
details.verseCommentary: The verse describes water descending from the sky and flowing in the valleys, reflecting the process of erosion and river flow, including underground systems, a phenomenon scientifically understood much later.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, rivers were observed, but their formation by erosion and the existence of underground rivers were not understood. Modern geomorphology studies make this Quranic description relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes water flowing in valleys.
Development of geomorphology and study of water erosion.
Discovery of karst systems and underground rivers.
Advanced mapping of river networks.

details.title: Shape of the Earth
details.scientificExplanation: The Earth is an oblate spheroid, a shape confirmed by observations such as those of Copernicus in the 16th century and modern satellite images. Its rotation causes a slight deformation, with an equatorial diameter larger than the polar diameter. This spherical shape explains the day-night cycle, where the Earth's rotation alternates exposure to the Sun.
details.arabicVerse: يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهَارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ النَّهَارَ عَلَى اللَّيْلِ
details.verseTranslation: He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'yukawwir' (wraps) suggests a spherical shape and rotational movement, corresponding to the Earth's rotation, which causes the alternation of day and night, a concept not fully understood in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the Earth was often considered flat in many cultures. The understanding of its spherical shape, confirmed by Copernicus and modern observations, makes the Quranic description significant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the wrapping of day and night.
Copernicus proposes a heliocentric model with a spherical Earth.
Satellite images confirm the Earth's oblate spheroid shape.
Precise measurements of the Earth's geoid.

details.title: Wind Patterns
details.scientificExplanation: Winds are caused by differences in atmospheric pressure due to the uneven heating of the Earth by the Sun. They carry pollen for plant pollination and moisture for cloud formation, contributing to precipitation. Studied by Halley in the 17th century, wind patterns, such as trade winds or jet streams, are essential for meteorology and ecosystems.
details.arabicVerse: وَأَرْسَلْنَا الرِّيَاحَ لَوَاقِحَ فَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً
details.verseTranslation: And We have sent the fertilizing winds, and sent down water from the sky.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'lawaqih' (fertilizing) describes winds as agents of pollination and bearers of rain, corresponding to the roles of winds in pollination and the water cycle, concepts scientifically understood later.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, winds were observed but their role in pollination and meteorology was not fully understood. Modern studies on winds make the Quranic description relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes winds as fertilizing.
Halley explains trade winds and wind patterns.
Discovery of jet streams and their meteorological role.
Advanced wind modeling via satellites.

details.title: Deserts and Rainfall
details.scientificExplanation: Rainfall can revitalize arid lands, such as deserts, by triggering the growth of temporary vegetation. This phenomenon, studied in desert ecology, depends on rare rains that activate dormant seeds, as in the Atacama Desert. Hydrological cycles and climate models, analyzed in the 20th century, explain how water transforms arid landscapes.
details.arabicVerse: وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنَّكَ تَرَى الْأَرْضَ خَاشِعَةً فَإِذَا أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا الْمَاءَ اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ
details.verseTranslation: And among His signs is that you see the earth barren, but when We send down rain upon it, it stirs and swells.
details.verseCommentary: The verse describes the revitalization of barren lands by rain, corresponding to the ecological phenomenon where water triggers growth in deserts, a process scientifically understood later.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the revitalization of deserts by rain was observed but not scientifically explained. Modern studies on desert ecology make this Quranic description relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the revitalization of land by rain.
Initial studies on desert ecology.
Discovery of seed dormancy cycles in deserts.
Satellite observations of desert transformations.

details.title: Ocean Currents
details.scientificExplanation: Ocean currents are large-scale movements of water, driven by winds, Earth's rotation, and density differences. Discovered by Benjamin Franklin in the 18th century, currents like the Gulf Stream transport heat and nutrients, influencing global climate. Deep currents, like those in abyssal oceans, are described as moving layers of water, similar to the Quranic description.
details.arabicVerse: أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ
details.verseTranslation: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by waves.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'bahr lujji' (deep sea) and the mention of waves suggest complex water movements, corresponding to deep ocean currents, a phenomenon studied scientifically long after the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, ocean currents were not scientifically understood. Modern observations of deep and surface currents make the Quranic description relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes movements in a deep sea.
Franklin charts the Gulf Stream.
Study of deep ocean currents.
Modeling of currents via oceanographic satellites.

details.title: Earth's Rotation
details.scientificExplanation: The Earth's rotation on its axis, completed in approximately 24 hours, causes the alternation of day and night. Confirmed by Galileo in the 17th century and measured precisely with modern clocks, this rotation is the origin of time zones and the Coriolis effect, influencing winds and ocean currents.
details.arabicVerse: يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهَارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ النَّهَارَ عَلَى اللَّيْلِ
details.verseTranslation: He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'yukawwir' (wraps) suggests a rotational movement, corresponding to the Earth's rotation which causes the alternation of day and night, a concept not fully understood in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, Earth's rotation was not recognized as the cause of the day-night cycle. The work of Galileo and modern observations confirm this Quranic description.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the wrapping of day and night.
Galileo supports Earth's rotation.
Foucault's pendulum proves Earth's rotation.
Precise measurements of rotation via GPS and satellites.

details.title: Mountains as Pegs
details.scientificExplanation: Mountains have deep roots that extend into the Earth's mantle, acting as 'pegs' to stabilize the Earth's crust. This concept, called isostasy, was proposed by George Airy in 1855. These roots, formed by plate tectonics, balance gravitational forces, reducing crustal oscillations. Modern geophysical studies confirm that mountain roots, like those of the Himalayas, extend tens of kilometers deep.
details.arabicVerse: وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا
details.verseTranslation: And the mountains as pegs.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'awtadan' (pegs) accurately describes the structure of mountain roots, which anchor mountains in the Earth's crust, corresponding to the scientific notion of isostasy.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, mountains were perceived as fixed structures, but their role as a geological anchor was unknown. The discovery of isostasy and mountain roots makes the Quranic description remarkable.

timeline.event: The Quran describes mountains as pegs.
Airy proposes the concept of isostasy.
Wegener develops the theory of plate tectonics.
Seismic imaging confirms the deep roots of mountains.

details.title: Layers of the Earth
details.scientificExplanation: The Earth is composed of several layers: the crust, mantle, outer core, and inner core. These layers, identified by seismic studies in the 20th century, vary in composition and density. The crust is thin (5-70 km), the mantle extends to about 2,900 km depth, and the core, primarily iron, reaches temperatures of 5,000 °C. These layers explain geological phenomena such as earthquakes and volcanism.
details.arabicVerse: اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ
details.verseTranslation: It is Allah who has created seven heavens and, from the Earth, their equivalent.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'from the Earth, their equivalent' can be interpreted as an allusion to the multiple internal layers of the Earth, corresponding to modern discoveries of the Earth's structure.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the internal structure of the Earth was unknown. Modern seismic studies, beginning with Inge Lehmann in 1936, confirm the Quranic description of the Earth's layers.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions the equivalent of the heavens for the Earth.
Lehmann discovers the Earth's inner core.
Improvement of seismic models of Earth's layers.
Advanced imaging of internal layers via seismic tomography.

details.title: Plate Tectonics
details.scientificExplanation: Plate tectonics, proposed by Alfred Wegener in 1915 and confirmed in the 1960s, explains the movement of lithospheric plates on the Earth's mantle. These movements, at a rate of a few centimeters per year, cause continental drift, mountain formation, and earthquakes. The plates move like 'clouds', in accordance with the verse's poetic imagery.
details.arabicVerse: وَتَرَى الْجِبَالَ تَحْسَبُهَا جَامِدَةً وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحَابِ
details.verseTranslation: And you see the mountains, you think them motionless, while they pass like the passing of clouds.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'like clouds' suggests a slow movement of the mountains, corresponding to the drift of tectonic plates, a concept unknown in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, mountains were considered fixed. The theory of plate tectonics, developed in the 20th century, makes the Quranic description of mountain movement significant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes mountains as moving.
Wegener proposes continental drift.
Confirmation of plate tectonics.
Precise mapping of plate movements via GPS.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of the movement of tectonic plates.

details.title: Rock Formation
details.scientificExplanation: Rocks are formed by three main processes: igneous (cooling of magma), sedimentary (accumulation and compaction of sediments), and metamorphic (transformation under pressure and heat). These processes, studied by James Hutton in the 18th century, are the origin of mountains and the Earth's crust. Mountains, formed mainly by tectonics, contain igneous and metamorphic rocks.
details.arabicVerse: وَالْأَرْضَ مَدَدْنَاهَا وَأَلْقَيْنَا فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ
details.verseTranslation: And the Earth, We have spread it out and placed therein firm mountains.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'rawasiya' (firm mountains) and 'madadnaha' (spread out) evokes the formation of rocks and mountains, corresponding to the geological processes of rock and crust formation.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, rock formation processes were unknown. The work of Hutton and modern geological studies make the Quranic description relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the creation of mountains.
Hutton establishes the foundations of modern geology.
Classification of igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks.
Advanced studies on petrogenesis.

details.title: Volcanic Activity
details.scientificExplanation: Volcanic activity results from the rise of magma from the Earth's mantle, leading to eruptions and the formation of new rocks. Studied by Georges Cuvier and others in the 19th century, it is linked to plate tectonics and releases gases and minerals into the atmosphere and crust. Volcanoes, like Vesuvius, show the power of the Earth's internal processes.
details.arabicVerse: إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا
details.verseTranslation: When the earth is shaken with its earthquake, And the earth discharges its burdens.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'discharges its burdens' can be interpreted as an allusion to magma and gases released during volcanic eruptions, corresponding to modern volcanic processes.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, volcanoes were observed, but their causes were unknown. Modern studies on volcanism make the Quranic description of the Earth's 'burdens' relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the Earth discharging its burdens.
Cuvier and others study volcanic processes.
Link between volcanism and plate tectonics.
Advanced volcanic monitoring via satellites.

details.title: Mineral Resources
details.scientificExplanation: The Earth contains mineral resources such as iron, copper, and gold, formed by geological processes such as volcanism and hydrothermal activity. Iron, for example, comes from sedimentary deposits or meteorites, as confirmed by isotopic analyses in the 20th century. These resources are essential for modern industries and have been exploited since antiquity.
details.arabicVerse: وَأَنزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ
details.verseTranslation: And We sent down iron, in which there is great strength.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'anzalna' (sent down) may refer to the cosmic origin of iron (meteorites) or its extraction from the Earth, corresponding to modern discoveries about mineral resources.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, iron was used, but its geological or cosmic origin was unknown. Modern mineral analyses make the Quranic description significant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions iron as 'sent down'.
Studies of mineral deposits and their formation.
Confirmation of the cosmic origin of iron.
Isotopic analysis of mineral resources.

details.title: Earth's Core
details.scientificExplanation: The Earth's core, composed of a liquid outer core and a solid inner core, primarily of iron and nickel, was discovered through seismic studies, notably by Inge Lehmann in 1936. The core generates the Earth's magnetic field via a dynamo effect and influences geological processes such as volcanism. Its depth reaches about 5,100 km, with temperatures approaching 5,000 °C.
details.arabicVerse: اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ
details.verseTranslation: It is Allah who has created seven heavens and, from the Earth, their equivalent.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'from the Earth, their equivalent' may symbolize the internal layers, including the core, corresponding to the complex structure of the Earth discovered by modern science.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the internal structure of the Earth, including the core, was unknown. Modern seismic discoveries make the Quranic reference to the Earth's layers significant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions the equivalent of the heavens for the Earth.
Lehmann discovers the Earth's inner core.
Detailed models of the core via seismology.
Advanced studies of the Earth's magnetic field.

details.title: Fossil Formation
details.scientificExplanation: Fossils form through the preservation of organism remains in sedimentary rocks, often through mineralization or rapid burial. Studied by William Smith in the 18th century, fossils reveal the history of life on Earth and are used to date geological layers. This process requires specific conditions, such as burial in fine sediments.
details.arabicVerse: ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِيَ كَالْحِجَارَةِ
details.verseTranslation: Then your hearts hardened after that, becoming like stones.
details.verseCommentary: Although metaphorical, the expression 'like stones' may evoke fossils embedded in rocks, corresponding to the fossilization process discovered by modern science.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, fossils were observed but their formation was not understood. Modern paleontology studies make the Quranic reference to 'stones' relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran compares hearts to stones.
Smith establishes the foundations of fossil stratigraphy.
Development of modern paleontology.
Fossil discoveries via advanced techniques.

diagrams.caption: Diagram of fossil preservation in rocks.

details.title: Earthquake Mechanisms
details.scientificExplanation: Earthquakes are caused by the release of accumulated energy along tectonic faults, due to the movement of lithospheric plates. Described by Charles Richter in the 1930s, they are measured by the Richter scale or the moment magnitude scale. Earthquakes, such as those on the San Andreas Fault, release seismic waves that shake the Earth.
details.arabicVerse: إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا
details.verseTranslation: When the earth is shaken with its earthquake.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'zulzilat' (shaken) accurately describes the effect of earthquakes, corresponding to the seismic movements caused by plate tectonics.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, earthquakes were observed but their tectonic causes were unknown. Modern seismological studies make the Quranic description relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the Earth shaken by an earthquake.
Richter develops the magnitude scale.
Confirmation of earthquakes related to plate tectonics.
Advanced seismic monitoring via global networks.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of an earthquake along a fault.
Diagram of seismic waves generated by an earthquake.

details.title: Mountain Ranges
details.scientificExplanation: Mountain ranges, such as the Himalayas or the Andes, form through the collision of tectonic plates, a process called orogeny. Studied by Eduard Suess in the 19th century, this phenomenon stabilizes the Earth's crust via isostasy. Mountain ranges influence climate and ecosystems, while reducing geological oscillations.
details.arabicVerse: وَأَلْقَىٰ فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ
details.verseTranslation: And He has placed in the earth firm mountains so that it does not shake with you.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'rawasiya' (firm mountains) and the idea of preventing shaking ('tamida') correspond to the function of mountain ranges in stabilizing the Earth's crust.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, mountains were seen as fixed structures. Discoveries about orogeny and isostasy make the Quranic description significant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes mountains as stabilizers.
Suess develops the theory of orogeny.
Confirmation of the role of plates in mountain formation.
Advanced studies on the impact of mountain ranges.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of the formation of a mountain range.

details.title: Ocean Currents and Barriers
details.scientificExplanation: Ocean currents are water flows separated by transition zones, such as ocean fronts or thermoclines, which act as natural barriers preventing the immediate mixing of water masses. Discovered by oceanographers like Matthew Maury in the 19th century, these barriers are due to differences in temperature, salinity, and density. For example, the Gulf Stream and North Atlantic waters meet without completely mixing, creating a visible boundary.
details.arabicVerse: مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ لَّا يَبْغِيَانِ
details.verseTranslation: He released the two seas, meeting; between them is a barrier they do not overpass.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'barzakh' (barrier) corresponds to ocean transition zones, such as fronts or pycnoclines, which prevent waters from mixing, a phenomenon studied scientifically long after the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, ocean currents and their barriers were unknown. Modern observations of ocean fronts make the Quranic description significant.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the barrier between two seas.
Maury publishes ocean current maps.
Study of ocean fronts and pycnoclines.
Satellite imagery of ocean barriers.

details.title: Darkness of the Sea Depths
details.scientificExplanation: Ocean depths, beyond 200 meters, are plunged into almost total darkness due to the absorption of light by water. Described by William Beebe during his dives in the 1930s, these zones, such as the aphotic zone, receive less than 1% of sunlight, creating a dark environment where life adapts via bioluminescence.
details.arabicVerse: أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ
details.verseTranslation: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by waves.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'bahr lujji' (deep sea) and 'zulumat' (darkness) accurately describe the darkness of the sea depths, a phenomenon unknown in the 7th century and confirmed by modern oceanography.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, ocean depths were inaccessible and their darkness unknown. Modern dives and submersibles confirm the Quranic description.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the darkness of the deep seas.
Beebe explores the ocean depths.
Trieste's dive into the Mariana Trench.
Mapping of aphotic zones via underwater robots.

details.videoTitle: Darkness of the Sea Depths: Quran and Oceanology

details.title: Ocean Waves
details.scientificExplanation: Ocean waves are generated by wind, tides, and earthquakes, creating complex movements such as internal or surface waves. Internal waves, studied in the 20th century, occur at the interface between water layers of different densities, forming 'waves upon waves'. This phenomenon, observed in areas such as the Strait of Gibraltar, influences ocean dynamics.
details.arabicVerse: أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ يَغْشَاهُ مَوْجٌ مِّن فَوْقِ مَوْجٍ
details.verseTranslation: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by a wave above a wave.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'wave above a wave' corresponds to internal and surface waves, a complex phenomenon accurately described in the Quran, long before its scientific understanding.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, surface waves were visible, but internal waves were unknown. Modern oceanographic studies confirm this Quranic description.

timeline.event: The Quran describes waves upon waves.
Discovery of ocean internal waves.
Advanced studies on wave dynamics.
Observation of internal waves via ocean sensors.

Diagram of surface and internal waves.

details.title: Salinity Gradients
details.scientificExplanation: Salinity gradients, or haloclines, separate fresh and salt waters in estuaries or confluence zones, such as the Mississippi Delta. These barriers, studied in the 20th century, prevent the immediate mixing of waters due to density differences. This phenomenon is observable where rivers meet the sea, maintaining a visible separation before gradual mixing.
details.arabicVerse: وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ وَهَٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ
details.verseTranslation: And it is He who has released the two seas: one fresh and sweet, the other salty and bitter.
details.verseCommentary: The terms 'adhbun furat' (fresh) and 'milhun ujaj' (salty) describe salinity gradients, corresponding to haloclines observed in estuaries, a phenomenon scientifically understood much later.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, salinity gradients were not scientifically understood. Modern observations of haloclines confirm the accuracy of the Quranic description.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the separation of fresh and salt waters.
Study of haloclines in estuaries.
Development of physical oceanography.
Mapping of salinity gradients via satellites.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of a halocline between fresh and salt water.
Diagram of a salinity gradient in an estuary.

details.title: Marine Ecosystems
details.scientificExplanation: Marine ecosystems, such as coral reefs and pelagic zones, support rich biodiversity, including fish, plankton, and marine mammals. Studied by Charles Darwin in the 19th century, these ecosystems depend on water to provide food and habitats. Marine food chains, based on phytoplankton, support edible species for humans, such as fish.
details.arabicVerse: وَهُوَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ الْبَحْرَ لِتَأْكُلُوا مِنْهُ لَحْمًا طَرِيًّا
details.verseTranslation: And it is He who has subjected the sea so that you may eat from it fresh meat.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'lahman tariyyan' (fresh meat) refers to the food resources of the oceans, corresponding to marine ecosystems that provide fish, a key food source.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, fishing was common, but the complexity of marine ecosystems was unknown. Modern studies on marine biodiversity make the Quranic description relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions the sea as a source of food.
Darwin studies marine ecosystems.
Development of marine ecology.
Mapping of marine ecosystems via satellites.

details.title: Ocean Resources
details.scientificExplanation: Oceans provide resources such as pearls, corals, and minerals, extracted through natural or human processes. Pearls, formed by mollusks, and corals, calcareous structures, have been used as ornaments since antiquity. Studied in the 19th century, these marine resources support coastal economies and cultures.
details.arabicVerse: وَتَسْتَخْرِجُوا مِنْهُ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَهَا
details.verseTranslation: And that you may extract from it ornaments to wear.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'hilyatan' (ornaments) refers to resources such as pearls and corals, corresponding to marine riches exploited for their beauty.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, pearls and corals were prized, but their biological formation was poorly understood. Modern studies on marine resources confirm the Quranic description.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions ornaments extracted from the sea.
Study of pearl and coral formation.
Sustainable exploitation of marine resources.
Analysis of marine deposits for minerals.

details.title: Tidal Movements
details.scientificExplanation: Tides are caused by the gravitational attraction of the Moon and the Sun, creating rhythmic movements of rising and falling ocean waters. Explained by Isaac Newton in the 17th century, tides follow predictable cycles, such as daily or monthly tides. These movements influence navigation and coastal ecosystems.
details.arabicVerse: الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ
details.verseTranslation: The sun and the moon follow a precise calculation.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'bihusban' (precise calculation) may include the rhythmic movements of tides, influenced by the Sun and Moon, a phenomenon scientifically understood long after the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, tides were observed, but their connection to lunar gravity was unknown. Newton's theories make the Quranic description relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions the precise calculation of the Sun and Moon.
Newton explains tides through gravitation.
Accurate tide predictions.
Tide modeling via satellites.

details.title: Maritime Navigation
details.scientificExplanation: Maritime navigation relies on understanding currents, winds, and tides, allowing ships to travel efficiently. Since antiquity, navigators used stars and winds, but advances in the 15th century, such as the compass and nautical charts, improved navigation. Modern ships use technologies like GPS to navigate the oceans.
details.arabicVerse: وَتَرَى الْفُلْكَ فِيهِ مَوَاخِرَ
details.verseTranslation: And you see the ships plowing through it.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'mawakhir' (plowing through) evokes maritime navigation, corresponding to the use of oceans for transport, an ancient practice but scientifically perfected later.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, navigation was common in the Arabian Peninsula, but modern tools like GPS were unknown. The Quranic description of ships remains relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions ships sailing on the sea.

Introduction of radar navigation.
Use of GPS for maritime navigation.

details.title: Ocean Depths
details.scientificExplanation: Ocean depths, such as the Mariana Trench (11 km), are extreme environments characterized by high pressure and total darkness. Explored by the Trieste in 1960, these zones host unique ecosystems adapted to extreme conditions, such as hydrothermal vents. The average ocean depth is about 3.7 km, with significant variations.
details.arabicVerse: أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُّجِّيٍّ
details.verseTranslation: Or like darkness in a deep sea.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'bahr lujji' (deep sea) accurately describes the ocean depths, corresponding to the abyssal zones studied by modern oceanography.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, ocean depths were inaccessible. Modern explorations of the abyss confirm the Quranic description of marine 'darkness'.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the darkness of the deep seas.
Trieste's dive into the Mariana Trench.
Discovery of deep-sea ecosystems.
Exploration of the abyss via submersibles.

details.title: Coral Reefs
details.scientificExplanation: Coral reefs, formed by the calcareous skeletons of coral polyps, are massive marine structures supporting exceptional biodiversity. Studied by Charles Darwin in the 19th century, reefs, such as the Great Barrier Reef, act as underwater 'mountains', influencing currents and protecting coastlines.
details.arabicVerse: وَلَهُ الْجَوَارِ الْمُنشَآتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَامِ
details.verseTranslation: And to Him belong the ships raised on the sea like mountains.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'ka-al-a'lam' (like mountains) may evoke coral reefs, massive structures visible underwater, corresponding to modern descriptions of reefs.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, coral reefs were observed by navigators, but their biological formation was unknown. Modern studies confirm their ecological role.

timeline.event: The Quran describes marine structures like mountains.
Darwin studies coral reef formation.
Discovery of the ecological role of reefs.
Reef monitoring via satellites.

details.title: Uniqueness of Fingerprints
details.scientificExplanation: Fingerprints are unique to each individual, formed by papillary ridges during embryonic development. Discovered by Francis Galton in the late 19th century, they are used in forensic medicine for identification. Their uniqueness stems from genetic and environmental variations in the womb, making each pattern distinct, even in identical twins.
details.arabicVerse: بَلَىٰ قَادِرِينَ عَلَىٰ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ
details.verseTranslation: Yes, We are able to reconstruct his fingertips.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'bananahu' (his fingertips) emphasizes the uniqueness of fingerprints, a concept unknown in the 7th century, but confirmed by modern discoveries in dermatoglyphics.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the uniqueness of fingerprints was not known. Galton's work and the use of fingerprints in criminology make the Quranic reference significant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions the reconstruction of fingers.
Galton publishes his work on fingerprints.
Adoption of fingerprints in forensic medicine.
Genetic analysis of papillary ridges.

details.title: Human Creation from Clay
details.scientificExplanation: Humans are composed of chemical elements such as carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and minerals, also present in clay. Clay contains silicates and metals essential to life, such as iron and magnesium. Research in biochemistry, particularly by Cairns-Smith in the 1980s, suggests that clay may have played a role in the origin of life by catalyzing prebiotic chemical reactions.
details.arabicVerse: الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ ۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلْقَ الْإِنسَانِ مِن طِينٍ
details.verseTranslation: He who perfected everything He created, and began the creation of man from clay.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'tin' (clay) may symbolize the chemical elements essential to life, corresponding to modern discoveries about the chemical composition of organisms and the potential role of clay in biogenesis.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the chemical composition of humans was unknown. Modern biochemical studies make the Quranic reference to clay relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions human creation from clay.
Discovery of chemical elements in organisms.
Cairns-Smith proposes the role of clay in the origin of life.
Advanced studies on prebiotic chemistry.

details.title: Genetic Diversity
details.scientificExplanation: Human genetic diversity results from variations in DNA, influencing traits such as skin color, language, and other characteristics. Discovered by Gregor Mendel in the 19th century and deepened by the Human Genome Project in the 1990s, this diversity is due to mutations, genetic recombinations, and environmental factors.
details.arabicVerse: وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ خَلْقُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافُ أَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَأَلْوَانِكُمْ
details.verseTranslation: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your languages and your colors.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'ikhtilaf alsinatikum wa alwanikum' (diversity of your languages and colors) reflects human genetic diversity, corresponding to genetic variations identified by modern genetics.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, human diversity was observable, but its genetic basis was unknown. Modern genetic discoveries make the Quranic description relevant.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions the diversity of languages and colors.
Mendel publishes his work on heredity.
Launch of the Human Genome Project.
Analysis of human genetic variations.
