details.title: Ease of Repeated Memorization
details.scientificExplanation: The repetition of the verse about ease of memorization in the Quran reinforces its accessibility, a phenomenon studied in neuroscience for its effect on memory retention.
details.arabicVerse: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
details.verseTranslation: And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
details.verseCommentary: The repetition of 'yassarna' (made easy) in several verses of Surah Al-Qamar emphasizes the Quran's design for easy memorization.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, oral memorization was crucial in a largely illiterate society, and repetition reinforced this practice.

timeline.event: The Quran repeats the ease of its memorization.
Studies on oral traditions and memorization.
Research on the neuroscience of memorization.

details.title: Winds as Rain Bearers
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes winds as bearers of clouds and rain, consistent with modern meteorology that explains their role in transporting moisture and forming precipitation.
details.arabicVerse: وَأَرْسَلْنَا الرِّيَاحَ لَوَاقِحَ فَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً
details.verseTranslation: And We have sent the fertilizing winds and sent down water from the sky.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'lawāqih' (fertilizing) illustrates the role of winds in the water cycle, emphasizing their function in creating rain, a sign of divine providence.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, in arid regions like Arabia, winds and rain were essential for survival, and their mention in the Quran reinforced recognition of divine power.

timeline.event: The Quran describes winds as rain bearers.
Development of meteorology and understanding of the water cycle.
Research on the role of winds in precipitation.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of winds as rain bearers.

details.title: Clouds as Water Reservoirs
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes clouds as water reservoirs, consistent with modern meteorology that explains cloud formation through condensation and their role in irrigating the earth.
details.arabicVerse: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُزْجِي سَحَابًا ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُ
details.verseTranslation: Do you not see that Allah drives clouds, then brings them together?
details.verseCommentary: The term 'yuzji sahaban' (drives clouds) describes the process of cloud formation, emphasizing their role as water reservoirs in the divine hydrological cycle.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, clouds and rain were perceived as signs of divine mercy, essential for agriculture in arid regions.

timeline.event: The Quran describes clouds as water reservoirs.
Studies on cloud formation and the water cycle.
Research on clouds and precipitation.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of clouds as water reservoirs.

details.title: Wisdom Behind Polygamy Up to Four Wives
details.scientificExplanation: The permission of polygamy, limited to four wives, aimed to address social needs, such as protecting widows and orphans in a tribal society. Biologically, females exhibit greater robustness at birth, with higher neonatal survival rates than males due to genetic factors like the double X chromosome, which protects against certain mutations. Additionally, modern demographic data shows a numerical predominance of women globally, with approximately 50.4% women versus 49.6% men (according to UN estimates for 2022), which may justify social structures like polygamy to balance needs in certain historical contexts.
details.arabicVerse: فَانكِحُوا مَا طَابَ لَكُم مِّنَ النِّسَاءِ مَثْنَىٰ وَثُلَاثَ وَرُبَاعَ ۖ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا فَوَاحِدَةً
details.verseTranslation: Marry women of your choice, two, three, or four; but if you fear that you will not be just, then only one.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'ta'dilu' (be just) imposes a strict condition of equity in the treatment of wives, emphasizing that monogamy is preferable if fairness cannot be guaranteed. This regulation reflects an implicit recognition of women's dignity and rights, in line with their demographic and biological importance in society.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, in a society where wars left many widows and orphans, polygamy provided social protection. The Quran limited this common practice to four wives while insisting on justice, in a context where women, often more numerous due to their biological resilience, required social support.

timeline.event: The Quran regulates polygamy with a limit of four wives, insisting on equity.
Studies on the role of polygamy in traditional societies and early demographic analyses showing female predominance.
Research on female biological robustness at birth and debates on gender equality in religious contexts.

diagrams.caption: Context of social reforms in Islam.

details.title: Site of Noah's Ark (Mount Ararat)
details.scientificExplanation: Archaeological explorations near Mount Ararat in Turkey have uncovered wooden artifacts and structures interpreted by some as remnants of Noah's Ark, though evidence remains debated. The region's geology shows sedimentary deposits consistent with ancient floods, corroborating flood narratives in multiple religious traditions.
details.arabicVerse: وَقِيلَ يَا أَرْضُ ابْلَعِي مَاءَكِ وَيَا سَمَاءُ أَقْلِعِي وَغِيضَ الْمَاءُ وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ
details.verseTranslation: And it was said: 'O earth, swallow your water! O sky, withhold!' The water subsided, the command was fulfilled, and the ark settled on Al-Judi.
details.verseCommentary: The verse mentions the ark resting on 'Al-Judi,' a term some associate with Mount Ararat. Archaeological finds, though inconclusive, fuel discussions on the historical accuracy of flood narratives.
details.historicalContext: Flood narratives exist in many cultures, including the Epic of Gilgamesh and biblical texts. Excavations near Mount Ararat, conducted since the 20th century, seek to link these accounts, though evidence remains controversial.

timeline.event: First modern explorations of Mount Ararat in search of the Ark.
Discovery of geological anomalies and wooden artifacts in the region.
Scientific debates on sedimentary deposits and flood narratives.

diagrams.caption: View of Mount Ararat, supposed site of the Ark.

details.title: City of Iram
details.scientificExplanation: Excavations in the 1990s in Oman uncovered structures at Ubar, identified as the legendary city of Iram mentioned in the Quran. Ebla tablets (2500-2250 BCE) mention similar names and places, suggesting a historical connection. Remote sensing technologies helped locate these buried remains.
details.arabicVerse: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ * إِرَمَ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ * الَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِي الْبِلَادِ
details.verseTranslation: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, * Iram of the pillars, * the like of which was never created in the lands?
details.verseCommentary: The term 'Iram dhat al-'imad' (Iram of the pillars) evokes a prosperous and technologically advanced city, destroyed for its arrogance. Discoveries at Ubar confirm the existence of a sophisticated city in the region.
details.historicalContext: Iram, associated with the tribe of 'Ad, is described as an opulent city in the Quran. Excavations at Ubar, conducted by international teams in the 1990s, revealed structures consistent with this description, corroborated by ancient texts like the Ebla tablets.

timeline.event: Ebla tablets mention names related to Iram.
Discovery of Ubar remains in Oman.
Use of remote sensing to confirm excavations.

details.videoTitle: Discovery of the City of Iram

details.title: Site of Al-Ula (Thamud)
details.scientificExplanation: Excavations at Al-Ula, Saudi Arabia, have uncovered Nabataean tombs and inscriptions linked to the Thamud tribe mentioned in the Quran. Stone structures and irrigation systems testify to an advanced civilization thriving in an arid environment.
details.arabicVerse: وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَالِحًا ۚ قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُ
details.verseTranslation: And to Thamud, their brother Salih. He said: 'O my people, worship Allah! You have no deity other than Him.'
details.verseCommentary: The Quran describes Thamud as a prosperous but rebellious tribe, punished for disobeying Prophet Salih. Remains at Al-Ula, especially Mada'in Salih, confirm an advanced society with monumental tombs.
details.historicalContext: Al-Ula, located on Nabataean trade routes, was a cultural and economic center. Excavations since the 2000s, supported by the Royal Commission for Al-Ula, have revealed remains dating from the 1st century BCE to the 1st century CE.

timeline.event: Peak of Nabataean civilization at Al-Ula.
Start of modern excavations at Al-Ula.
Discovery of new inscriptions and tombs by the Royal Commission for Al-Ula.

details.title: Preserved Body of Ramses II
details.scientificExplanation: The mummy of Ramses II, discovered in 1881 at Deir el-Bahri, is remarkably preserved due to Egyptian embalming techniques. The Quran mentions the preservation of Pharaoh's body as a sign, corresponding to the exceptional state of the mummy studied by modern Egyptologists.
details.arabicVerse: فَالْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنْ خَلْفَكَ آيَةً
details.verseTranslation: So today We will save you in body that you may be a sign for those who come after you.
details.verseCommentary: The verse suggests that Pharaoh's body, identified by some as Ramses II, would be preserved as a divine sign. The discovery of his mummy in 1881 reinforced this interpretation, though the precise link remains debated.
details.historicalContext: Ramses II, pharaoh of the 19th Dynasty (1279-1213 BCE), is known for his military exploits and role in the biblical and Quranic Exodus. The discovery of his mummy advanced understanding of Egyptian funerary practices.

timeline.event: Reign of Ramses II in Egypt.
Discovery of Ramses II's mummy at Deir el-Bahri.
Scientific analyses of Egyptian embalming techniques.

details.title: Ebla Tablets
details.scientificExplanation: The Ebla tablets, discovered in 1975 in Syria and dated 2500-2250 BCE, contain references to names and places mentioned in the Quran, such as Iram. These cuneiform texts confirm the existence of ancient civilizations in the region, supporting Quranic narratives.
details.arabicVerse: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ * إِرَمَ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ * الَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِي الْبِلَادِ
details.verseTranslation: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, * Iram of the pillars, * the like of which was never created in the lands?
details.verseCommentary: The Ebla tablets mention names similar to those in the Quran, such as 'Iram,' suggesting a historical memory of ancient civilizations. These discoveries enhance the credibility of Quranic accounts of lost peoples.
details.historicalContext: Ebla was a major trade center in the 3rd millennium BCE. The tablets, discovered by an Italian team, contain administrative and religious information, linking Quranic narratives to a concrete archaeological context.

timeline.event: Writing of the Ebla tablets.
Discovery of the tablets by an Italian team.
Analysis of tablets to establish links with Quranic narratives.

details.title: Inscriptions of Khaybar
details.scientificExplanation: Excavations at Khaybar, Saudi Arabia, have revealed fortifications, canals, and inscriptions from the 7th century, confirming a prosperous Jewish community mentioned in the Quran. Recent research (2020-2022) shows continuous human occupation since prehistory.
details.arabicVerse: وَأَوْرَثَكُمْ أَرْضَهُمْ وَدِيَارَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ وَأَرْضًا لَّمْ تَطَئُوهَا
details.verseTranslation: And He caused you to inherit their land, their dwellings, their wealth, and a land you had not trodden.
details.verseCommentary: The verse refers to the Battle of Khaybar (628 CE), where Muslim forces defeated a local Jewish community. Excavations confirm fortifications and complex social organization at that time.
details.historicalContext: Khaybar, 150 km north of Medina, was a strategic oasis. Franco-Saudi excavations (2020-2022) uncovered prehistoric and historical structures, confirming its importance as a settlement center.

timeline.event: Battle of Khaybar between Muslims and Jewish community.
Excavations of the Khaybar Longue Durée Archaeological Project.
Publication of initial findings on Khaybar's landscape organization.

details.title: The Sleepers in the Cave
details.scientificExplanation: The narrative of the Sleepers in the Cave, known as the 'Seven Sleepers of Ephesus' in Christian tradition, describes youths sleeping for centuries in a cave. Archaeological excavations near Ephesus, Turkey, have uncovered caves and tombs associated with this story, dating to the Roman period (2nd-5th century CE), though the miraculous nature remains theological. The verse states that God turned them from side to side according to the sun to preserve their bodies. In medical science, for patients in prolonged coma, regular turning prevents bedsores caused by prolonged pressure on the skin. Intensive care studies show this practice, recommended every 2 hours, reduces the risk of tissue necrosis. Additionally, alternating sun exposure could regulate circadian rhythms, though in coma, biological functions are altered.
details.arabicVerse: أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْكَهْفِ وَالرَّقِيمِ كَانُوا مِنْ آيَاتِنَا عَجَبًا
details.verseTranslation: Or have you thought that the people of the Cave and Ar-Raqim were a wonder among Our signs?
details.verseCommentary: The verse introduces the story of youths who, fleeing persecution, were protected by God in a cave. Excavations at Ephesus uncovered a cave with Christian inscriptions, associated with this narrative, though the 309-year sleep remains a miracle.
details.historicalContext: The Sleepers narrative is shared with Christian tradition, likely dating to the 3rd century CE under Emperor Decius. 19th-century excavations at Ephesus revealed a cave and church dedicated to the Seven Sleepers, confirming veneration of the site in Byzantine times.

timeline.event: Presumed persecution of the youths under Emperor Decius.
Discovery of the Seven Sleepers' cave at Ephesus.
Archaeological studies on sites linked to the Sleepers.

diagrams.caption: Cave of the Seven Sleepers at Ephesus.
Archaeological context of the Roman period.

details.title: The Traveler and the Resurrected Animal
details.scientificExplanation: The story of the traveler whose donkey is decomposed and then reconstituted defies biological laws of decay and resurrection. Though without direct archaeological evidence, sites like Jericho or ancient ruins in Palestine have been explored for links to destroyed cities, without specific confirmation.
details.arabicVerse: أَوْ كَالَّذِي مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا
details.verseTranslation: Or like the one who passed by a city in ruins, asking how God could revive it.
details.verseCommentary: The verse describes a miracle where God causes the traveler and his donkey to die, then resurrects them after 100 years, illustrating divine power over life and death. Archaeological explorations of ancient cities like Jericho show layers of destruction and rebuilding, though not directly linked to the verse.
details.historicalContext: The narrative draws from Jewish traditions about Ezra or other figures, adapted in the Quran to teach resurrection. Excavations at Jericho, one of the oldest known cities, reveal destruction and reconstruction layers, though not directly related to the verse.

timeline.event: Ruins of cities like Jericho dating back to 8000 BCE.
Initial excavations at Jericho by European archaeologists.
Studies on resurrection narratives in religious traditions.

details.title: The Riches of Qarun
details.scientificExplanation: Qarun (Korah in the Bible) is swallowed with his treasures, a symbolic narrative of the impermanence of wealth. Though without direct archaeological evidence, ancient Egyptian sites show buried treasures, and geological studies on earthquakes could explain similar engulfments.
details.arabicVerse: إِنَّ قَارُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ
details.verseTranslation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he oppressed them.
details.verseCommentary: The verse describes Qarun as a wealthy and arrogant man, punished by the engulfment of his house and treasures. Archaeological discoveries in Egypt, such as rich tombs, illustrate the opulence of the era, though the engulfment is a miraculous event without archaeological trace.
details.historicalContext: Qarun is associated with the time of Moses (around 1300 BCE). Excavations in Egypt reveal gold and jewelry treasures from the pharaonic era, reflecting the described wealth, but the engulfment is a miraculous event without archaeological trace.

timeline.event: Presumed era of Qarun under Moses.
Excavations in Egypt revealing pharaonic treasures.
Studies on divine punishment narratives in religious traditions.

details.title: The King Who Challenged Ibrahim
details.scientificExplanation: The story of Nimrod challenging Abraham is theological, but Sumerian and Assyrian inscriptions mention kings like Nimrod, associated with legendary figures. Excavations at Ur and Babylon reveal royal palaces, although the specific debate is symbolic.
details.arabicVerse: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ
details.verseTranslation: Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord?
details.verseCommentary: The verse describes an arrogant king (Nimrod) challenging Abraham about resurrection, humiliated by a divine demonstration. Mesopotamian artifacts, such as royal steles, show kings claiming divine power, similar to Nimrod.
details.historicalContext: Nimrod is a legendary figure in Mesopotamian traditions (2000 BCE), associated with the construction of the Tower of Babel. Excavations at Nimrud (Kalhu) in Iraq have revealed Assyrian palaces, although the direct link with Nimrod remains legendary.

timeline.event: Presumed era of Nimrod and Abraham.
Excavations at Nimrud by Austen Henry Layard.
Studies on Mesopotamian royal figures.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of the debate between the king and Abraham.

details.title: The Two Brothers and the Harvests
details.scientificExplanation: The story of the two brothers (Cain and Abel in the Bible) involves murder and a crow teaching burial. Excavations in Israel and Jordan have revealed ancient agricultural sites with harvesting tools, although the story remains symbolic without direct evidence.
details.arabicVerse: وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ابْنَيْ آدَمَ بِالْحَقِّ
details.verseTranslation: Recite to them the true story of the two sons of Adam.
details.verseCommentary: The verse recounts the murder by the jealous brother and divine teaching through a crow to bury the body. Bronze Age agricultural artifacts in Palestine show similar harvesting practices, although the miracle remains theological.
details.historicalContext: The story of the two brothers is shared with biblical traditions (Genesis 4). Excavations at Tell es-Sultan (Jericho) reveal agricultural sites dating back to 9000 BCE, providing historical context to harvest stories, although not directly related.

timeline.event: Stories of Cain and Abel in Abrahamic traditions.
Agricultural excavations at Jericho.
Studies on the origins of fratricide stories.

details.title: Musa and the Divine Scholar
details.scientificExplanation: The story of Moses and Al-Khidr involves miraculous acts like piercing a boat or rebuilding a wall. Although without direct archaeological evidence, sites like the Al-Khidr Mosque in Turkey or Palestine are associated with popular traditions, although their authenticity is folkloric.
details.arabicVerse: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِفَتَاهُ لَا أَبْرَحُ حَتَّىٰ أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ
details.verseTranslation: And when Moses said to his servant, 'I will not cease until I reach the junction of the two seas.'
details.verseCommentary: The verse recounts the wisdom lessons given to Moses by Al-Khidr, with miraculous acts explained later. Sites like the Bosphorus confluence have been proposed, but excavations have not revealed direct evidence, the story being spiritual.
details.historicalContext: Al-Khidr is a mystical figure in Islamic traditions, associated with immortality. Sanctuaries in Turkey and the Middle East, dating from the Middle Ages, testify to popular veneration, although without ancient artifacts related to the story.

timeline.event: Construction of sanctuaries dedicated to Al-Khidr.
Studies on mystical figures in Islam.
Debates on potential sites of 'majma' al-bahrayn' (junction of the two seas).

details.title: The Queen of Sheba
details.scientificExplanation: The story of the Queen of Sheba and Solomon involves miracles like the transportation of the throne. Excavations in Yemen and Ethiopia have revealed sites like Marib, with Sabaean temples and inscriptions, confirming an advanced civilization in the 10th century BCE.
details.arabicVerse: وَتَفَقَّدَ الطَّيْرَ فَقَالَ مَا لِيَ لَا أَرَى الْهُدْهُدَ
details.verseTranslation: He inspected the birds and said, 'Why do I not see the hoopoe?'
details.verseCommentary: The verse describes Solomon communicating with animals and the Queen of Sheba converting after miracles. Sabaean inscriptions from Marib mention queens and trade, aligned with the Quranic narrative.
details.historicalContext: The Queen of Sheba is associated with Bilqis, ruling the kingdom of Saba (Yemen). Excavations at Marib, the Sabaean capital, revealed a dam and temples dating from the 8th century BCE, illustrating a civilization rich in trade.

timeline.event: Presumed reign of the Queen of Sheba.
Excavations at Marib by American and Yemeni archaeologists.
Studies on Sabaean inscriptions and links with biblical and Quranic narratives.

diagrams.caption: Remains of the kingdom of Saba at Marib.

details.title: Sulayman and the Miraculous Horses
details.scientificExplanation: The story of Solomon inspecting his miraculous horses is theological, but excavations in Israel have revealed royal stables at Megiddo, dating from the 9th century BCE, associated with Solomon's reign, with structures for hundreds of horses.
details.arabicVerse: إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَشِيِّ الصَّافِنَاتُ الْجِيَادُ
details.verseTranslation: When, at evening, prancing horses were presented to him.
details.verseCommentary: The verse describes Solomon admiring his horses, a sign of his divine wealth. The stables at Megiddo confirm the importance of horses in Solomon's kingdom, although the miracle remains spiritual.
details.historicalContext: Solomon (10th century BCE) is known for his prosperous kingdom. Excavations at Megiddo, conducted since the 20th century, revealed stables for 450 horses, corroborating stories of equestrian wealth.

timeline.event: Reign of Solomon and construction of stables.
Excavations at Megiddo by the University of Chicago.
Studies on royal stables and links with biblical and Quranic narratives.

details.title: The Child Defending His Mother
details.scientificExplanation: The miracle of Jesus speaking from the cradle is theological, without direct archaeological evidence. Sites like Bethlehem and Nazareth have revealed remains from the Roman era, although the story remains miraculous without specific artifacts.
details.arabicVerse: فَأَتَتْ بِهِ قَوْمَهَا تَحْمِلُهُ ۖ قَالُوا يَا مَرْيَمُ لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْئًا فَرِيًّا
details.verseTranslation: She came to her people carrying him. They said, 'O Mary, you have certainly done a strange thing!'
details.verseCommentary: The verse describes Jesus defending Mary by speaking from the cradle, a miracle confirming his prophecy. Excavations in Bethlehem, such as the Church of the Nativity, date from the Byzantine era but reflect historical veneration of Jesus' birthplace.
details.historicalContext: The story of Mary and Jesus is shared with Christian traditions (Infancy Gospel). Excavations in Bethlehem and Nazareth, conducted since the 19th century, have revealed religious sites dating from the Roman era, although the miracle is spiritual.

timeline.event: Presumed birth of Jesus in Bethlehem.
Initial excavations in Bethlehem and Nazareth.
Studies on ancient Christian sites in Palestine.

details.title: The Lowest Point on Earth
details.scientificExplanation: The verse mentions the defeat of the Romans at the 'lowest point on earth,' identified as the Dead Sea region (-427 meters below sea level). Excavations in the region have revealed Byzantine battle sites, such as near the Sea of Galilee, confirming historical events.
details.arabicVerse: غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ ۝ فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ
details.verseTranslation: The Romans have been defeated * In the nearest land.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'adni al-ard' (the nearest/lowest land) refers to the Dead Sea region, the lowest point on earth. Archaeological discoveries, such as Byzantine artifacts, corroborate battles in this area in the 7th century.
details.historicalContext: The Byzantine defeat against the Persians (613-614 CE) occurred near the Dead Sea. Excavations at Ayn Gharandal and other sites reveal Roman and Byzantine fortifications, although the precise link with the verse is interpretive.

timeline.event: Byzantine defeat against the Persians near the Dead Sea.
Geographical and archaeological excavations around the Dead Sea.
Scientific confirmation of the lowest point on earth.

details.title: Unique Fingerprints
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran draws attention to fingerprints, specifying that it is easy for God to resurrect man after death. Fingerprints are absolutely unique to each person. Every individual living or having lived on earth has unique fingerprints. This characteristic was discovered only towards the end of the 19th century. Before that, people considered fingerprints as ordinary lines without particular importance. The Quran, revealed in the 7th century, emphasizes this uniqueness long before its scientific discovery, serving as an 'identity card' in modern criminology.
details.arabicVerse: بَلَىٰ قَادِرِينَ عَلَىٰ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ
details.verseTranslation: Yes, We are able to reconstruct even the tips of his fingers.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'banan' refers to the fingertips, where fingerprints are located. The verse emphasizes God's ability to reconstruct even unique details like fingerprints during resurrection, illustrating divine precision.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, fingerprints were unknown as unique identifiers. Their uniqueness was discovered in the 19th century, making the Quranic mention remarkable. The Quran uses this to prove the possibility of resurrection.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions the uniqueness of fingertips.
Discovery of fingerprint uniqueness by Sir William Herschel.
Use of fingerprints in criminology as an identification method.

details.title: Seas That Do Not Mix
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes a barrier between two seas preventing their mixing, a phenomenon observed in estuaries and confirmed by oceanography. Winds floating in the air with the particles they carry from the sea, which then allows the formation of rain clouds. If winds did not have this property, water droplets would not form. This corresponds to the phenomenon of pycnocline or halocline, where waters of different densities do not mix.
details.arabicVerse: مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ ۝ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ لَّا يَبْغِيَانِ
details.verseTranslation: He released the two seas, meeting * Between them is a barrier they do not overpass.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'barzakh' (barrier) refers to an invisible separation between two bodies of water, illustrating the divine power to control natural elements.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, this phenomenon was not scientifically understood. The Quran describes it accurately, a fact confirmed by modern oceanography.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the barrier between seas.
Scientific discovery of halocline.
Studies on estuaries and marine barriers.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of seas that do not mix.

details.title: Haman as Pharaoh's Architect
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran names Haman as a builder for Pharaoh. Contrary to expectations, the name Haman is never mentioned in the Torah sections concerning Moses' life. However, we encounter Haman in the later chapters of the Old Testament, presented as an assistant to a Babylonian king. With the deciphering of hieroglyphs, an important reality was discovered: the name 'Haman' was indeed mentioned in Egyptian inscriptions. This name was given to a monument dating from the Pharaonic era. In the dictionary People in the New Kingdom, based on all inscriptions, Haman is mentioned as 'the chief of the stone quarry workers.' The result revealed an important truth. Unlike the false claims of the Quran's critics, Haman was a person who lived in Egypt during the time of Moses and was close to Pharaoh. In conclusion, the existence of the name Haman in ancient Egyptian inscriptions not only invalidated the claims of the Quran's critics but also confirmed once again that the Quran comes from God. Moreover, the Quran provides historical information that could not have been known or understood during the Prophet's era.
details.arabicVerse: وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِي فَأَوْقِدْ لِي يَا هَامَانُ عَلَى الطِّينِ
details.verseTranslation: Pharaoh said: 'O notables, I know of no god for you other than myself. Haman, light a fire for me on the clay to make bricks.'
details.verseCommentary: The term 'Haman' refers to a close assistant of Pharaoh in charge of construction. The discovery of his name in Egyptian hieroglyphs confirms his historical existence, unknown during the Prophet's time.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the name 'Haman' was not known as an advisor to Pharaoh in Jewish or Christian traditions. Its mention in the Quran, confirmed by Egyptian inscriptions deciphered in the 19th century, shows advanced historical knowledge.

timeline.event: Era of Moses and Pharaoh, where Haman was chief of stone quarries.
Deciphering of Egyptian hieroglyphs revealing the name Haman.
Publication of dictionaries confirming Haman as a historical figure.

details.title: Big Bang Theory
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes the heavens and the earth as a united mass before their separation, aligning with the Big Bang theory. This event, known as the 'Big Bang,' produced the entire Universe about 15 billion years ago, creating it from nothing. Before the Big Bang, there was no such thing as matter. From nothingness where there was neither matter, nor energy, nor time, nor space, this great explosion occurred, giving rise to the entire Universe. The matter and energy contained in the universe were united in a single point. The universe formed following a great explosion that took place outside of time. Before the Big Bang, celestial matter existed in the form of gaseous matter. Scientists compare the expanding Universe to a great explosion that occurred outside of time.
details.arabicVerse: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا
details.verseTranslation: Have those who disbelieved not seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity? Then We separated them.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'ratq' (joined entity) and 'fataq' (separated) describe the origin of the universe as a unity before its expansion, a concept aligned with the Big Bang.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the idea of a universe originating from a united mass was unknown. The Quran describes it accurately, a fact confirmed by modern astronomy in the 20th century.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the origin of the universe as a separated mass.
Formulation of the Big Bang theory by Georges Lemaître.
Confirmation by cosmic observations such as the cosmic microwave background.

details.title: Expansion of the Universe
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran states that the heavens are being expanded, corresponding to the observed cosmic expansion. The Universe has been constantly expanding since the Big Bang. Scientists compare the expanding Universe to a great explosion that took place outside of time. From the moment of the Big Bang, the Universe has been in constant expansion.
details.arabicVerse: وَالسَّمَاءَ بَنَيْنَاهَا بِأَيْدٍ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ
details.verseTranslation: And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'musi'un' (expander) denotes the continuous expansion of the heavens, a concept aligned with the universe's expansion discovered in the 20th century.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the idea of an expanding universe was unknown. The Quran describes it accurately, a fact confirmed by modern astronomy.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the expansion of the heavens.
Discovery of the universe's expansion by Edwin Hubble.
Confirmation by observations such as the Hubble telescope.

details.title: Spherical Shape of the Earth
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes the night wrapping around the day, indicating the roundness of the Earth. This corresponds to the spherical shape of the Earth, scientifically discovered in the 16th century, though mentioned in the Quran in the 7th century.
details.arabicVerse: خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ ۖ يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهَارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ النَّهَارَ عَلَى اللَّيْلِ
details.verseTranslation: He created the heavens and earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'yukawwir' (wraps) describes the overlapping of day and night, possible only on a spherical Earth.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the notion of a flat Earth was widespread. The Quran accurately describes the spherical shape, a fact confirmed by modern science.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the spherical shape of the Earth.
Magellan confirms the roundness of the Earth by circumnavigation.
Space observations confirm the geoid shape.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of the Earth's spherical shape.

details.title: Reflected Light of the Moon
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes the moon as reflected light, distinct from the sun's own light. This fact, mentioned in the 7th century, corresponds to the modern understanding that the moon reflects sunlight, scientifically confirmed in modern times.
details.arabicVerse: تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ بُرُوجًا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَاجًا وَقَمَرًا مُنِيرًا
details.verseTranslation: Blessed is He who has placed in the sky great stars and placed therein a [burning] lamp and luminous moon.
details.verseCommentary: The term 'munir' (luminous) indicates that the moon reflects light, unlike the sun, described as 'siraj' (lamp), which produces its own light.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the distinction between the moon's reflected light and the sun's own light was not commonly accepted. The Quran specifies it, a fact validated by modern science.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the moon as reflected light.
Scientific confirmation that the moon reflects sunlight.
Telescopic observations and lunar missions confirm light reflection.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of the moon's reflected light.

details.title: Celestial Origin of Iron
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran states that iron was 'sent down,' corresponding to the meteoritic origin of iron, formed in stars and brought to Earth by meteorites. Modern science has confirmed that iron is produced by stellar nucleosynthesis and dispersed by supernovae, a concept studied in the 20th century.
details.arabicVerse: وَأَنزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ
details.verseTranslation: And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for the people.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'anzalna al-hadid' (sent down iron) reflects the extraterrestrial origin of iron, a fact validated by astrophysical discoveries on nucleosynthesis.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the meteoritic origin of iron was unknown. The Quran anticipates this knowledge, confirmed by modern scientific observations.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions iron being sent down.
Discovery of stellar nucleosynthesis.
Confirmation by spectroscopic analyses of meteorites.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of the meteoritic origin of iron.

details.title: Pairs in Creation
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran mentions that everything is created in pairs, anticipating biological duality (male/female) and physical duality (particle/antiparticle). Modern biology has confirmed sexual reproduction, and quantum physics discovered matter/antimatter pairs in the 20th century.
details.arabicVerse: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنبِتُ الْأَرْضُ وَمِنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
details.verseTranslation: Exalted is He who created all pairs – from what the earth grows and from themselves and from that which they do not know.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'al-azwaj kullaha' (all pairs) encompasses biological and physical duality, validated by modern biology and physics.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the notion of pairs in biology and physics was unknown. The Quran anticipates this duality, confirmed by modern science.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions creation in pairs.
Discovery of sexual reproduction in biology.
Discovery of matter/antimatter pairs in physics.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of biological and physical duality.

details.title: Relativity of Time
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes a day equivalent to a thousand years, reflecting the relativity of time, a concept aligned with Einstein's theory of relativity. Time dilation has been confirmed by experiments in the 20th century.
details.arabicVerse: يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ
details.verseTranslation: He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'yawm kan miqdaruhu alf sanah' (a day equivalent to a thousand years) anticipates the relativity of time, validated by Einstein's theory.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the relativity of time was unknown. The Quran anticipates this concept, confirmed by modern physics.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the relativity of time.
Theory of relativity by Albert Einstein.
Confirmation by experiments on time dilation.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of the relativity of time.

details.title: Protected Vault of the Atmosphere
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes the sky as a protected vault, corresponding to the ozone layer and atmosphere that protect the Earth from solar radiation. This protective role was studied by modern science in the 20th century.
details.arabicVerse: وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَّحْفُوظًا
details.verseTranslation: And We made the sky a protected ceiling.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'saqf mahfuz' (protected vault) reflects the role of the atmosphere, particularly the ozone layer, validated by modern science.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the protective role of the atmosphere was unknown. The Quran anticipates this function, confirmed by atmospheric studies.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the sky as a protected vault.
Discovery of the ozone layer by Charles Fabry.
Confirmation by satellite observations.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of the atmosphere's protective role.

details.title: Mountains as Pegs
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran compares mountains to pegs, reflecting their role in tectonic stability by anchoring the Earth's crust. This concept was studied by modern geology in the 20th century.
details.arabicVerse: وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا
details.verseTranslation: And the mountains as stakes.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'jibal awtad' (mountains as pegs) reflects the deep roots of mountains, validated by plate tectonics.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the role of mountains in tectonic stability was unknown. The Quran anticipates this concept, confirmed by geological studies.

timeline.event: The Quran compares mountains to pegs.
Discovery of mountain roots by plate tectonics.
Confirmation by geophysical studies.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of mountains as tectonic pegs.

details.title: Embryological Stages
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes the stages of embryonic development (nutfah, alaqah, mudghah, bones, flesh) with remarkable precision, corresponding to the stages identified by modern embryology in the 20th century.
details.arabicVerse: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنسَانَ مِن سُلَالَةٍ مِّن طِينٍ ۝ ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُطْفَةً فِي قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍ ۝ ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْمُضْغَةَ عِظَامًا فَكَسَوْنَا الْعِظَامَ لَحْمًا ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ ۚ فَتَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ
details.verseTranslation: We created man from an extract of clay. Then We made him as a drop in a place of settlement, firmly fixed. Then We made the drop into an alaqah (leech-like structure), then We made the alaqah into a mudghah (chewed-like substance), then We made the mudghah into bones, and clothed the bones with flesh, then We developed him into another creation. So blessed is Allah, the Best of Creators.
details.verseCommentary: The terms 'nutfah', 'alaqah', and 'mudghah' precisely describe embryonic stages, validated by modern embryology.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, embryonic stages were unknown. The Quran anticipates these stages, confirmed by modern science.

timeline.event: The Quran describes embryological stages.
Discovery of embryonic stages by modern embryology.
Confirmation by medical imaging techniques.

details.title: Pain Receptors in the Skin
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran indicates that the skin is the seat of pain, corresponding to pain receptors (nociceptors) discovered in modern anatomy. These receptors were studied in the 20th century.
details.arabicVerse: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِنَا سَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِمْ نَارًا كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُم بَدَّلْنَاهُمْ جُلُودًا غَيْرَهَا لِيَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ
details.verseTranslation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses - We will drive them into a fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'juluduhum' (their skin) emphasizes the role of the skin in pain perception, validated by the discovery of nociceptors.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the role of pain receptors was not known. The Quran anticipates this knowledge, confirmed by modern anatomy.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions the skin as the seat of pain.
Discovery of nociceptors by neurobiology.
Confirmation through neurological studies.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of pain receptors in the skin.

details.title: Water Cycle
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes the hydrological cycle, including rain, springs, and vegetation, corresponding to the water cycle studied by modern geography in the 18th century.
details.arabicVerse: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَسَلَكَهُ يَنَابِيعَ فِي الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعًا مُّخْتَلِفًا أَلْوَانُهُ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَاهُ مُصْفَرًّا ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ حُطَامًا ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ
details.verseTranslation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky, making it flow as springs in the earth; then He produces thereby crops of varying colors; then they dry and you see them turned yellow; then He makes them debris. Indeed, in that is a reminder for those of understanding.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'anzala min as-sama' ma'' (sends down water from the sky) describes the hydrological cycle, validated by modern geography.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the water cycle was not understood. The Quran anticipates this process, confirmed by modern hydrological studies.

timeline.event: The Quran describes the water cycle.
Studies on the hydrological cycle by Pierre Perrault.
Confirmation through modern hydrological analysis.

details.title: Plants Created in Pairs
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran mentions that plants are created in male-female pairs, corresponding to the sexual reproduction of plants discovered by modern botany in the 18th century.
details.arabicVerse: الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا مِّن نَّبَاتٍ شَتَّىٰ
details.verseTranslation: He who has made for you the earth as a bed and inserted therein for you roadways and sent down from the sky rain and produced thereby pairs of various plants.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'azwaj min nabat' (pairs of plants) reflects the sexual reproduction of plants, validated by modern botany.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the sexual reproduction of plants was not known. The Quran anticipates this concept, confirmed by botanical studies.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions plants created in pairs.
Discovery of plant sexual reproduction by Carl Linnaeus.
Confirmation through modern botanical studies.

details.title: Healing Through Honey
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes honey as a remedy, corresponding to its antibacterial and antioxidant properties confirmed by modern medicine in the 20th century.
details.arabicVerse: يَخْرُجُ مِن بُطُونِهَا شَرَابٌ مُّخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهُ فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ لِّلنَّاسِ
details.verseTranslation: There emerges from their bellies a drink, varying in colors, in which there is healing for people.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'fihi shifa' lil-nas' (healing for people) reflects the medicinal properties of honey, validated by modern medicine.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the medicinal properties of honey were not scientifically established. The Quran anticipates this benefit, confirmed by modern studies.

timeline.event: The Quran describes honey as a remedy.
Discovery of honey's antibacterial properties.
Confirmation through modern medical studies.

details.title: Ant Communication
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran mentions an ant communicating, corresponding to the discovery of pheromones and social behaviors of ants by modern ethology in the 20th century.
details.arabicVerse: حَتَّىٰ إِذَا أَتَوْا عَلَىٰ وَادِ النَّمْلِ قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ
details.verseTranslation: Until when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said, 'O ants, enter your dwellings.'
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'qalat namlah' (an ant said) reflects ant communication through pheromones, validated by modern ethology.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, ant communication was not known. The Quran anticipates this behavior, confirmed by ethological studies.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions an ant communicating.
Discovery of pheromones by Jean-Henri Fabre.
Confirmation through modern ethological studies.

details.title: Fragility of Spider Web
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran compares the spider web to a weak structure, reflecting its physical reality. Although strong for its size, spider silk is fragile against external forces, a fact studied by modern zoology in the 20th century.
details.arabicVerse: مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ كَمَثَلِ الْعَنكَبُوتِ اتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتًا
details.verseTranslation: The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like that of the spider who takes a home.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'kamathal al-ankabut ittakhadhat baytan' (like the spider who takes a home) reflects the relative fragility of the spider web, validated by studies on spider silk.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the structure and fragility of spider webs were not scientifically studied. The Quran anticipates this observation, confirmed by modern zoology.

timeline.event: The Quran compares the spider web to a weak structure.
Studies on the mechanical properties of spider silk.
Confirmation through modern biomechanical analysis.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of the fragile structure of spider web.

details.title: Preservation of Pharaoh's Body
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran predicts the preservation of Pharaoh's body as a sign, confirmed by the discovery of Ramses II's mummy, preserved through Egyptian embalming techniques studied in the 19th century.
details.arabicVerse: فَالْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنْ خَلْفَكَ آيَةً
details.verseTranslation: So today We will save you in your body that you may be a sign for those after you.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'nunajjika bibadanik' (save you in your body) reflects the preservation of Pharaoh's body, validated by the discovery of Ramses II's mummy.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, Egyptian embalming techniques were not known in Arabia. The Quran anticipates this preservation, confirmed by modern archaeology.

timeline.event: The Quran predicts the preservation of Pharaoh's body.
Discovery of Ramses II's mummy.
Confirmation through modern archaeological analysis.

details.title: Lowest Point on Earth
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran mentions a defeat at the 'lowest point on earth,' corresponding to the Dead Sea region, located about -400 meters below sea level, confirmed by modern geology.
details.arabicVerse: فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُم مِّن بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ
details.verseTranslation: In the lowest part of the earth, and they, after their defeat, will be victorious.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'adna al-ard' (lowest part of the earth) refers to the Dead Sea, validated by modern geographical surveys.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the exact topography of the Dead Sea was not known. The Quran anticipates this observation, confirmed by modern geology.

timeline.event: The Quran mentions the lowest point on earth.
Topographic measurements of the Dead Sea.
Confirmation through modern geological surveys.

details.title: Orbits of Celestial Bodies
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes the sun and moon following orbits, anticipating modern astronomy's discoveries about the orbital trajectories of celestial bodies, confirmed in the 17th century by Kepler.
details.arabicVerse: وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ ۖ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ
details.verseTranslation: And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all in an orbit are swimming.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'kullun fi falakin yasbahun' (all in an orbit are swimming) reflects the elliptical orbits of celestial bodies, validated by modern astronomy.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the orbits of celestial bodies were not understood. The Quran anticipates this concept, confirmed by Kepler's laws.

timeline.event: The Quran describes orbits of celestial bodies.
Laws of planetary orbits by Johannes Kepler.
Confirmation through modern astronomical observations.

details.title: Frontal Lobe and Lying
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran links lying to the forehead, corresponding to the frontal lobe, where modern neurobiology locates decision-making and ethical control functions, studied in the 20th century.
details.arabicVerse: كَلَّا لَئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنَّاصِيَةِ ۝ نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ
details.verseTranslation: No! If he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock - A lying, sinning forelock.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'nasiyatin kadhibatin khati'atin' (lying, sinning forelock) reflects the role of the frontal lobe in lying, validated by modern neurobiology.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the role of the frontal lobe in behavior was not known. The Quran anticipates this discovery, confirmed by modern science.

timeline.event: The Quran links lying to the forehead.
Discovery of the frontal lobe's role by neurobiology.
Confirmation through brain imaging studies.

details.title: Creation from Water
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran states that all life is created from water, a fundamental principle in biology, confirming that water is essential to life, discovered in the 19th century.
details.arabicVerse: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ
details.verseTranslation: And We made from water every living thing.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'min al-ma’i kulla shay’in hayy' (from water every living thing) reflects the essential role of water in life, validated by modern biology.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the central role of water in life was not scientifically established. The Quran anticipates this principle, confirmed by biology.

timeline.event: The Quran states that life is created from water.
Discovery of the role of water in biology.
Confirmation by modern biological studies.

diagrams.caption: Illustration of the role of water in life.

details.title: Barrier Between Fresh and Salt Waters
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran describes a barrier between fresh and salt waters, corresponding to the halocline phenomenon, where differences in salinity prevent mixing, studied by modern oceanography in the 20th century.

details.verseTranslation: And it is He who has released [simultaneously] the two seas, one fresh and sweet and one salty and bitter, and He placed between them a barrier and prohibiting partition.
details.verseCommentary: The expression 'barzakhan wahijran mahjuran' (barrier and prohibiting partition) reflects the halocline, validated by modern oceanography.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, the halocline phenomenon was unknown. The Quran anticipates this observation, confirmed by oceanographic studies.

details.title: White Hair Due to Intense Stress
details.scientificExplanation: Surah Al-Muzzammil (73:17) describes a phenomenon where children's hair turns white due to extreme stress—a sign of the Day of Resurrection. Modern science confirms that intense stress can cause sudden hair whitening, known as canities subita. Studies published in *Nature* in 2020 show that acute stress activates the sympathetic nervous system, leading to rapid loss of melanocytes responsible for hair pigmentation. Though rare, this is documented in cases of extreme psychological stress.
details.arabicVerse: فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِن كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًا يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدَانَ شِيبًا
details.verseTranslation: Then how will you protect yourselves, if you disbelieve, from a Day that will make the children white-haired?
details.verseCommentary: Verse 73:17 describes the Day of Resurrection as so terrifying that even children's hair will turn white. This reference to extreme stress is remarkable, as modern science only recently identified this phenomenon, validating the Quran's precision in describing the physiological effects of trauma.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, Quranic descriptions of apocalyptic signs, such as hair whitening due to fear, were powerful imagery to reinforce belief in the Hereafter. At the time, the biological mechanisms of stress were unknown, making this reference especially striking in light of modern discoveries.

timeline.event: Revelation of the Quran describing children's hair turning white as a sign of the Day of Resurrection.
Early medical studies on the effects of stress on human physiology.

details.verseCommentary: The term 'al-afaq' (horizons) encompasses the observable universe, while 'anfusihim' (themselves) includes human biology. This verse anticipates modern scientific discoveries, such as cosmic expansion or genetics, revealing the complex order of creation.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, scientific knowledge was limited, making this invitation to exploration remarkable. Modern scientific advances, such as the discovery of cosmic and biological laws, resonate with this Quranic challenge.

details.title: Challenge of Exploring the Heavens and Earth's Depths
details.scientificExplanation: The Quran challenges humans and jinn to penetrate the mysteries of the heavens and Earth's depths without 'authority' (sultan). Modern science shows that space exploration (Apollo, Voyager missions) and geological drilling (Kola Superdeep Borehole, Russia) are limited by technological and energy constraints, requiring colossal resources—in resonance with the Quranic idea of human limitation without divine aid.
details.arabicVerse: يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنسِ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَن تَنفُذُوا مِنْ أَقْطَارِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانفُذُوا ۚ لَا تَنفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطَانٍ
details.verseTranslation: O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except by authority [from Allah].
details.verseCommentary: The term 'aqtari as-samawat' (regions of the heavens) and 'al-ard' (the earth) evoke the limits of human exploration. Current challenges in space and deep-earth exploration, such as energy costs and physical barriers, reflect this idea of human limitation.
details.historicalContext: In the 7th century, exploring the heavens or Earth's depths was inconceivable. This Quranic challenge anticipates modern efforts in astronomy and geology, where human limits remain evident despite technological advances.

timeline.event: Revelation of the Quran challenging exploration of the heavens and the earth.
Apollo 11 mission: first human moon landing.
Kola Superdeep Borehole, the deepest geological well (12.3 km).
